nodes.name: Controlled-fire pyrotechnology
nodes.auditRationale: Root of the pyrotechnology family with seven dependents; no prerequisite is needed (fire itself is baseline, D-047 ruling 2). Effect is food security from earth-oven processing, kept distinct from the lamp's underground-light role.
nodes.effectRationale: Managed hearths and earth ovens make tough roots, seeds and bone grease edible: a wider fallback diet lets a band absorb lean seasons.

nodes.name: Oldowan flaking
nodes.auditRationale: Root of the knapping family; unchanged. Effect is food-security from butchery and marrow, not tool output.
nodes.effectRationale: Sharp flakes and hammerstones open carcasses and long bones: marrow and scavenged meat let a band ride out lean spells.

nodes.name: Prepared-core (Levallois)
nodes.auditRationale: Levallois is a prepared-core refinement of hard-hammer flaking; making knapping_oldowan its prerequisite gives the knapping family one root instead of two unrelated roots (both A1, Oldowan ~2.6 Mya precedes ~300 kya). Not a chronology edge: the prepared core is literally flaking applied with foresight.
nodes.effectRationale: Prepared cores yield predetermined, portable blanks: groups carry a toolkit instead of tethering to a stone source, so movers range further.

nodes.name: Blade production
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Blade cores are a further development of prepared-core reduction.

nodes.effectRationale: Prismatic blade cores give several times more cutting edge per kilogram of flint: quarrying and working stone yields more usable product per worker.

nodes.name: Pressure flaking
nodes.auditRationale: Currently an isolated root and leaf. The Blombos evidence ties the two directly: silcrete was heat-treated precisely so it could be pressure-flaked (~75 kya, after heat treatment at ~164 kya). Pressure retouch of a fine blank presupposes improving the stone first. Remains a deliberate leaf (finishing technique).
nodes.effectRationale: Thin, symmetrical projectile points (Solutrean, Clovis) make big-game kills more reliable, so lean seasons kill fewer.

nodes.name: Heat treatment of stone
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Becomes a non-leaf if pressure_flaking takes it as prerequisite.

prereqAssessment.why: Controlled heating in a sand bed under a fire is the method.
The heated stone is then knapped by prepared-core methods; Levallois (~300 kya) precedes Pinnacle Point (~164 kya).

nodes.effectRationale: Heating poor silcrete or chert makes it flake cleanly: more of the quarried stone becomes usable, and the resulting edges are sharper.

nodes.name: Microliths and composite tools
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Microliths are useless unless set in a haft.
Microliths are snapped and backed blade segments.

nodes.effectRationale: Replaceable geometric inserts: a worn or broken segment is swapped and the sickle or knife lives on, so equipped tools last longer.

nodes.name: Ground-edge axe
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; live unlock activity.logging plus a housing labour effect from efficient woodworking.

prereqAssessment.why: Ground axes are first roughed out by flaking, then ground; flaking is the needed predecessor.

nodes.effectRationale: A resharpenable ground-edge felling axe makes heavy timber work feasible: logging is unlocked and dwellings take less labour.

nodes.name: Compound adhesives
nodes.auditRationale: Root; keep. fire_making is NOT added despite heat-processed bitumen: its node is dated ~164 kya, after this node's ~200 kya, which would break chronology.
nodes.effectRationale: Load-bearing compound binders keep inserts and heads seated under impact: tools fail less and transmit more force.

nodes.name: Birch-bark tar
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Birch tar is the manufactured successor of natural binders.
Dry distillation needs controlled heating without oxygen.

nodes.effectRationale: Tar is an adhesive and a wood and bark preservative and sealant: treated timber and bark structures last longer.

nodes.name: Composite hafting
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. unit.spearmen requires it but units are not live (M7), so the realized effect is the tool-yield operand.

prereqAssessment.why: Compound adhesive is the other half of a load-bearing haft.
Sinew or fibre binding of the haft.

nodes.effectRationale: A precision-fitted socket or tang turns a hand-held edge into a lever: hafted axes, adzes and hoes multiply the gain from every tool.

nodes.name: Cordage
nodes.auditRationale: Correct root: fibre twisting has no technical precursor beyond hands and plants. Hub node with 11 dependents; keep.

nodes.name: Basketry
nodes.auditRationale: Causal prerequisite is right. The live unlock (infra.fish_weir) is its main effect; a small storage effect gives the container role its own weight.

prereqAssessment.why: Coiled and twined basketry uses the same twisting and binding of fibre that cordage establishes.

nodes.name: Spear-thrower
nodes.auditRationale: Sound A1 root of ranged hunting; feeds the war_band civic. Small food-security effect, distinct from the bow (range of movement) and sling (herds).

prereqAssessment.why: The dart is a hafted point; the thrower is a lever for a hafted projectile.

nodes.effectRationale: Large game taken at range is a reserve when gathered food fails: a band absorbs a lean season instead of going hungry.

nodes.name: Simple bow
nodes.auditRationale: Keep: the bow is the root of four later bows and feeds war_band. Units are not live, so the effect is the bow's provisioning role for parties on the move.

prereqAssessment.why: A bow is useless without a strong fibre string; cordage is the binding requirement.

nodes.effectRationale: Bow hunters feed themselves on the move from small and medium game, so a scouting party can push each step further into unknown ground.

nodes.name: Sling
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Effect follows the node's own capability (herd protection); it only bites once herding exists.

prereqAssessment.why: The sling is two cords and a pouch.

nodes.effectRationale: The sling is the shepherd's weapon: predators and thieves are driven off at range, so herds lose fewer animals.

nodes.name: Framed hut
nodes.auditRationale: Minimal and correct prerequisite; the frame is the bridge to timber_frame.

prereqAssessment.why: Framed huts are lashed together; without cordage there is no frame of poles or bones.

nodes.name: Hide working
nodes.auditRationale: Correct causal prerequisite (cross-lane to materials, same Age).

prereqAssessment.why: Hide scrapers are prepared-core flake tools; the Middle Palaeolithic scraper kit is what makes systematic hide work possible.

nodes.name: Eyed needle and sewing
nodes.auditRationale: AND is right: both the material (hide) and the thread are required. The node is the cold-climate expansion enabler, so its effect is on migration reach.

prereqAssessment.why: Fitted garments are sewn from prepared hides and furs.
Sewing needs thread or sinew twisted into cord.

nodes.name: Sea-crossing raft
nodes.auditRationale: Correct causal prerequisite; the first open-water crossing is an exploration-range capability, not a cargo one.

prereqAssessment.why: Logs or reed bundles stay together only when lashed; cordage (~50 kya) is the one material precondition of a raft that survives open water.

nodes.name: Load-carrying dugout
nodes.auditRationale: Both atoms are genuine working requirements; river freight is the dugout's causal effect.

prereqAssessment.why: Dugouts were hollowed by alternate charring and scraping; controlled fire is the working method (Pesse).
Ground-edge axes and adzes fell and shape the log; both are needed, so AND is right.

nodes.name: Line and pelagic fishing
nodes.auditRationale: Correct, minimal causal prerequisite. Leaf is deliberate: later commercial fishing grows from nets, salt and ships (new node herring_buss), not from the hook.

prereqAssessment.why: Line fishing needs twisted fibre line; shell and bone hooks are useless without it.

nodes.name: Grinding stone
nodes.auditRationale: Root node with no prerequisite is right (Upper Palaeolithic plant processing needs only stone).

nodes.name: Dog domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Root node is right. One dependent edge (pig) is replaced, see pig; sheep_goat keeps it.

nodes.name: Pigment processing
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Blombos ochre was processed on grindstones; the edge is the actual technique.

nodes.effectRationale: Ground ochre for body marking and shared symbolic display builds group identity, damping the build-up of grievance; also preserves hides.

nodes.name: Bone and antler tools
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Groove-and-splinter bone working needs burins struck from blades.

nodes.effectRationale: Eyed needles and awls make tailored, layered clothing; less exposure lowers baseline mortality (harpoons also add fish).

nodes.name: Oil lamp
nodes.auditRationale: Keep its own prerequisite. It is a leaf today, but underground mining needs light: propose that mining_shaft (T2, A3) gains lamp as a prerequisite (chalk-cut lamps at Grimes Graves, Spiennes-type flint shafts). Routed to the integrator, not applied from this record.

prereqAssessment.why: A fat lamp is a controlled, sustained small flame; it presupposes deliberate fire management.

nodes.effectRationale: Portable light makes underground work possible: ochre and flint mining (Lion Cave ~40 kya; chalk-cut lamps in Neolithic flint mines) depend on it.

nodes.name: Tally marks
nodes.auditRationale: Sound root of the numeracy chain (three dependents across science and communication). Kept; small food-security effect, distinct from the calendar's sowing effect.

prereqAssessment.why: The marks are incised into bone with stone and bone tools; Lebombo and Ishango are notched bones.

nodes.effectRationale: Counting days and stored portions beyond memory lets a band ration ahead of a lean moon: shortfalls are absorbed instead of becoming hunger.

nodes.name: Cereal cultivation
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Hub node; prerequisite is causal.

prereqAssessment.why: Natufian ground-stone processing of wild cereals preceded and made worthwhile their deliberate sowing.

nodes.name: Wheat and barley domestication
nodes.auditRationale: The node's description makes sickle harvesting the mechanism of domestication, yet sickle has no dependents. Adding it closes a missing bridge and gives the sickle a downstream role. sickle (~12,500 BCE) predates the node (~9,500 BCE).

prereqAssessment.why: Domestication is the genetic outcome of centuries of cultivation.
ADDED: sickle reaping of ripe-but-unshattered ears is the selection pressure that fixed the non-shattering rachis (the node's own description).

nodes.name: Wet rice cultivation
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Irrigation is not required: Kuahuqiao and Tianluoshan paddies precede canal systems.

prereqAssessment.why: Generic cultivation knowledge; paddy rice is an independent centre but the node models the practice, not the genome.

nodes.name: Millet cultivation
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Same cultivation practice applied to Panicum and Setaria.

nodes.name: Maize domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Keep prerequisite; flag cost only.

prereqAssessment.why: Cultivation practice; teosinte-to-maize took millennia of tending.

nodes.name: African cereal domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; Age label noted, not moved.

prereqAssessment.why: Cultivation practice applied to Sahelian grasses.

nodes.name: Root and tuber cultivation
nodes.auditRationale: Keep with no prerequisite: vegetative propagation (Kuk, Andes) arose independently of seed agriculture and grinding.

nodes.name: Legume cultivation
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Pulses were co-domesticated with cereals in the same field systems.

nodes.name: Fruit tree cultivation
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; OR is right (either sedentary farming path).

prereqAssessment.why: Sedentary cultivators can make multi-decade perennial investments.
Equally valid for vegeculture societies (bananas, breadfruit).

nodes.name: Sickle
nodes.auditRationale: Leaf today although it is the mechanism of cereal domestication; becomes a prerequisite of cereal_domesticated (see that record).

prereqAssessment.why: Natufian sickles were microlith blades set in bone or wood hafts.

nodes.name: Hoe
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: A hoe is a hafted blade.
Neolithic hoe blades were ground stone.

nodes.name: Nixtamalization
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Deliberate leaf: a health capability that changes mortality, not a gateway.

prereqAssessment.why: The process exists only for maize.
Alkaline cooking at the ~1,500 BCE date is pottery-based.

nodes.name: Sheep and goat domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: The first managed animal relationship precedes herd management; weak but harmless, and it is the only route into herding.

nodes.name: Cattle domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Near Eastern cattle were domesticated by communities already managing caprines.

nodes.name: Pig domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Replace the non-causal dog edge with sedentary cultivation (~11,500 BCE predates ~8,500 BCE).

prereqAssessment.why: Dogs play no role in pig domestication. Pigs were domesticated as scavengers of sedentary cultivating villages (Cayonu ~8,500 BCE; Jiahu), so the causal prerequisite is cereal_cultivation.

nodes.name: Milking and dairying
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; (sheep_goat OR cattle) AND pottery is right.

prereqAssessment.why: Earliest dairying is on caprines.
Equally on cattle.
Milk lipids in pottery are the evidence; vessels make cheese and yoghurt possible.

nodes.name: Wool sheep and fleece
nodes.auditRationale: Keep: the sheep_goat atom is essential; cordage is weak but not wrong and removing it would change nothing material.

prereqAssessment.why: Woolly fleece is a product of selective breeding of domestic sheep.
Weak but harmless: fleece was selected because fibre could already be twisted into yarn; it keeps the fibre logic of the lane.

nodes.name: Animal traction
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Oxen were the first draught animals.

nodes.name: Open-fired pottery
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; live recipe plus storage and child-feeding effects. Fire is baseline (baseline.fire), so no fire_making edge is needed.

prereqAssessment.why: Coil building and container design come from basketry; many early pots carry basket impressions.

nodes.effectRationale: Sealed pots keep stores from damp and vermin; boiling makes gruels that wean and feed children through shortages.

nodes.name: Updraft kiln

future.system: Construction - kiln (deferred-entity plan, tier A)
future.description: a built kiln fires pottery in greater volume for less fuel

nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Kiln chambers are built of mudbrick and clay.
The kiln is an enclosed version of pottery firing.

nodes.effectRationale: Live unlock building.kiln; the kiln's own building effects carry the gameplay, so no operand is added.

nodes.name: Fast wheel (throwing)
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf (a craft specialisation). Emerged ~3,500 BCE sits on the A2/A3 boundary; Age kept.

prereqAssessment.why: Throwing presupposes ceramic know-how.

nodes.effectRationale: Thrown pottery at scale is a full-time trade: the wheel supports a larger specialist artisan class.

nodes.name: Mudbrick
nodes.auditRationale: Root is defensible: moulded earth bricks need no prior technique in the tree. The live unlock (building.city_wall) is kept; the timber saving is its housing role.

nodes.name: Lime plaster
nodes.auditRationale: Correct, minimal causal prerequisite (cross-lane to energy, A1 to A2).

prereqAssessment.why: Quicklime is made by burning limestone at ~800 C; controlled fire is the causal precursor.

nodes.name: Timber-frame construction
nodes.auditRationale: Correct AND. After the loom change it still has four dependents (canal_lock, track_road, traction_trebuchet, well).

prereqAssessment.why: Ground stone axes and adzes fell and shape the posts and beams.
The framed hut is the direct structural ancestor of the post-and-beam house.

nodes.name: Dry-stone construction
nodes.auditRationale: Correct. Hub for walls, harbour and built roads (all live).

prereqAssessment.why: Pecked and ground stone working is the precursor of fitted unmortared stone.

nodes.name: Dug well
nodes.auditRationale: OR is right: either lining technique suffices.

prereqAssessment.why: Stone-lined shafts (Atlit-Yam) are one way to keep a well open.
Timber-lined shafts (LBK oak wells) are the other.

nodes.name: Grain fermentation (beer)
nodes.prereq: (cereal_domesticated OR rice_wet OR millet OR maize OR sorghum_pearl_millet) AND pottery_open_fired
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; the OR over any cereal is right.

prereqAssessment.why: Barley and wheat beer.
Rice wine.
Millet beer.
Chicha.
Sorghum beer.
Malting and brewing at scale need vessels.

nodes.name: Wine and fruit fermentation
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. orchard is not required: early fruit wines used wild fruit and honey.

prereqAssessment.why: Jiahu and Georgian wine residues are in pottery jars.

nodes.name: Oil pressing

future.system: Production chains - oil press (deferred-entity plan, tier D)
future.description: a press turns olives, sesame and flax into oil for food and lamps; no oil good exists in this build

nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Olive cultivation supplies the fruit.
Stone press beds and crushing basins.

nodes.name: Salt production
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Briquetage: brine evaporated in coarse pottery (Poiana Slatinei).

nodes.name: Flax cultivation
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Flax was cultivated in the Levantine founder-crop package.

nodes.name: Spindle spinning
nodes.prereq: cordage AND (flax OR wool OR cotton_cultivation)
nodes.auditRationale: cordage AND (any fibre) is the right shape: any one spinnable fibre suffices.

prereqAssessment.why: The spindle mechanises the twisting that cordage does by hand.
One of three alternative fibre sources; OR is right.
Alternative fibre source; OR is right.
Alternative fibre source; OR is right.

nodes.name: Warp-weighted loom
nodes.auditRationale: Remove timber_frame: not causal, and dated 1,500 years after the node's own emerged date (contract §6 chronology). The textile workshop it requires (inst.textile_workshop) is not live, so the node gets a specialist-class effect.

prereqAssessment.why: A loom needs spun thread for the warp.

A warp-weighted loom is two uprights and a beam leaned on a wall; it does not need post-and-beam house joinery. Chronology also fails: Çatalhöyük textiles (~7,000 BCE) predate LBK timber framing (~5,500 BCE).

nodes.name: Dyeing
nodes.auditRationale: Correct AND; A1 ochre to A2 dyeing is a reasonable cross-Age chain.

prereqAssessment.why: Dye is applied to fibre and thread; spun fibre is what is dyed.
Mineral pigment preparation is the precursor of dye and mordant chemistry.

nodes.name: Native copper working
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Annealing between hammerings needs fire.
Native copper is worked with hammerstones and grinding, a ground-stone skill set.

nodes.effectRationale: Cold-hammered and annealed copper awls, pins and small blades: a first metal edge for equipped workers.

nodes.name: Copper smelting
nodes.prereq: kiln_updraft AND charcoal AND (copper_native OR ochre_processing)
nodes.auditRationale: Reduction smelting needs charcoal: its carbon monoxide is the reductant and a wood fire cannot reach or hold reducing conditions. The node's own description says 'in a charcoal fire'. charcoal (A2, ~5,500 BCE) predates smelting (~5,000 BCE); charcoal already feeds iron_bloomery on the same grounds.

prereqAssessment.why: Knowing copper as a material; OR branch.
Furnace temperatures and atmosphere control come from kilns.
Malachite and azurite were ground as pigment before they were smelted; the OR alternative is a real pathway.

nodes.effectRationale: Smelted metal can be resharpened and remelted instead of discarded: tools last longer; smithy unlocked.

nodes.name: Charcoal making
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are sound. Its only dependent is iron_bloomery; T2 has already proposed copper_smelting += charcoal, which closes the obvious missing edge (smelting needs a reducing fuel).

prereqAssessment.why: Tar making is pyrolysis of wood in a sealed, oxygen-starved pit: the same principle as a covered charcoal pile.
Felling and splitting the cordwood for a clamp needs ground-edge axes.

nodes.effectRationale: Charcoal carries about twice the heat of firewood per load, so a settlement can draw its fuel from further out: pre-industrial cities ringed themselves with charcoal-burning zones beyond the firewood belt.

nodes.name: Open-mould casting
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Casting needs molten metal from smelting.

nodes.effectRationale: Cast copper axe heads are reproducible: felling and quarrying crews are better equipped.

nodes.name: Native gold and silver
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Same cold-working and annealing techniques as native copper.

nodes.effectRationale: Gold and silver as prestige goods and an early store of value: exchange is easier, so price gaps close faster.

nodes.name: Basin irrigation
nodes.auditRationale: OR over staple crops is right.

prereqAssessment.why: Floodplain basins were built for cereal fields.
Alternative cultivated base; OR is right.

nodes.name: Canal irrigation
nodes.auditRationale: OR over staples is right; surveying (A3) is not required for the Samarran canals.

prereqAssessment.why: Canal irrigation served cereal fields.
Alternative cultivated base; OR is right.

nodes.name: Agricultural terracing
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Leaf is deliberate: the capability is the infrastructure.

prereqAssessment.why: Terrace risers are dry-stone walls.
Seed farming on slopes.
Andean and New Guinea tuber terraces.

nodes.name: Sledge
nodes.auditRationale: A self-contained hauling capability; the wheel supersedes it for most loads, so a leaf is deliberate.

prereqAssessment.why: Runners and crossbars are shaped with ground-stone axes and adzes (Heinola runner).

nodes.name: Solid wheel and axle
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are causal; the wheel is the transport hub of the Bronze Age tree.

prereqAssessment.why: The earliest wheeled vehicles (Bronocice, Uruk pictographs) are ox-drawn; the wheel has no use without a draught animal.
Plank wheels and axles were cut with stone woodworking tools (Ljubljana Marshes wheel).

nodes.name: Ox cart
nodes.auditRationale: Kept as the vehicle node; its effect (hinterland reach) is distinct from the wheel's (bulk haulage cost).

prereqAssessment.why: The ox cart is the wheel and axle under a load bed; the draught animal comes through wheel_solid.

nodes.name: Trackway
nodes.auditRationale: Live unlock of the path tier (road_track) and, with stone_dry / horse_domestication, of built roads and courier relays. Proposed as a prerequisite of road_paved (see that record), which makes it a bridge rather than a leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: The Sweet Track is split planks pinned with pegs across a marsh: carpentry of the timber-frame tradition.

nodes.name: Ard plough
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: The ard is drawn by oxen.
The ard is a dragged hoe; tillage-tool lineage.

nodes.name: Clay tokens
nodes.auditRationale: Causal prerequisites correct (Schmandt-Besserat token thesis). The capability is stores accounting, so the effect sits on famine relief rather than on yield.

prereqAssessment.why: Most Near Eastern tokens are baked clay; firing makes the counters durable enough to be kept, stored and enclosed in bullae.
One-mark-one-unit counting (Lebombo, Ishango) is the abstraction a token generalises to commodity-specific counters.

nodes.name: Stamp seal
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites correct. inst.archive is not live, so the node needs an operand effect; storeroom sealing reduces store losses.

prereqAssessment.why: Seals are carved and ground stone; the grinding and drilling repertoire of ground-edge tools is the working technique.
Sealings are impressions in clay on jars, bales and storeroom doors; a clay-working tradition is the medium (Halaf sealings on vessel stoppers).

nodes.name: Lunar calendar
nodes.auditRationale: Correct single bridge from tally to the calendars and astronomy; five dependents. Kept.

prereqAssessment.why: A month count is a tally of lunations; the Lebombo and Ishango notches are read as lunar counts.

nodes.effectRationale: Sowing and harvest timed by counted months avoid plantings lost to early frost or late rain: steadier harvests.

nodes.name: Trepanation
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: a Neolithic surgical practice with no line to later medicine.

prereqAssessment.why: Flint blades cut the skull.

nodes.effectRationale: Many trepanations treated depressed skull fractures; healed edges show survival above 50%.

nodes.name: Arsenical bronze
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: the no-tin alloy path. Emerged ~4,000 BCE predates the A3 window, as do several A3 materials nodes placed by maturity; Age not moved.

prereqAssessment.why: Smelted from arsenical ores in the same furnaces.

nodes.effectRationale: Arsenic-bearing copper work-hardens: harder edges without tin trade.

nodes.name: Tin bronze
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Tin ore (cassiterite) must be found before it can be alloyed; copper smelting comes through this atom.

nodes.effectRationale: A reproducible 10% tin alloy is harder and work-hardens: edges hold far longer than copper; bronze casting unlocked.

nodes.name: Two-piece and closed-mould casting
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Closed moulds extend open-mould casting.
Bronze's fluidity fills thin bivalve moulds for socketed forms.

nodes.effectRationale: Bivalve moulds turn out socketed sickles and hoes that stay on their hafts: each farmer harvests and tills more.

nodes.name: Lost-wax casting
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf (art and ritual metalwork).

prereqAssessment.why: Investment casting needs pouring skills.

nodes.effectRationale: Cult statuary and votive objects in any shape sustain shared ritual and display.

nodes.name: Sheet metalwork
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Its main capability (sheet armour) is military and not live; the realized effect is a modest food-handling one.

prereqAssessment.why: Raising sheet relies on bronze's work-hardening and annealing behaviour.

nodes.effectRationale: Raised bronze cauldrons and buckets let households and feasts cook and redistribute stores in bulk; armour use waits for M7.

nodes.name: Shaft mining
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: The node models ore mining for metal; flint mines predate it but are not its capability.
Shoring, stone-lined galleries and spoil handling.

nodes.effectRationale: Shafts and galleries follow ore to depth: sustained extraction per miner; the mining activity joins Extraction.

nodes.name: Proto-cuneiform
nodes.auditRationale: Single causal prerequisite is the accepted derivation; effect is fiscal accounting, its documented use.

prereqAssessment.why: Proto-cuneiform signs for commodities and numbers derive from the token repertoire impressed on bullae (Uruk IV).

nodes.name: Cuneiform (full writing)
nodes.auditRationale: Correct derivation. Library and school are live; the operand captures the specific use of cuneiform for long-distance correspondence.

prereqAssessment.why: Full cuneiform grew directly out of proto-cuneiform by phonetic (rebus) extension (~2,900 BCE).

nodes.name: Egyptian hieroglyphic
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisite acceptable and does not force a Mesopotamian dependency for an Egyptian route. Effect differs from cuneiform (reach) by being the specialist-class capacity.

prereqAssessment.why: Egyptian writing begins as commodity labels and numerals (Abydos U-j tags); a record-of-quantity tradition is the shared precursor, whether independent or stimulus-diffused.

nodes.name: Oracle bone script
nodes.auditRationale: Independent East Asian origin is correctly not routed through Mesopotamia. Effect is the observational record, distinct from the other scripts.

prereqAssessment.why: Numerals and count marks precede and survive into oracle-bone numerals; the generic notation precursor.
The medium is prepared scapulae and plastrons, drilled and inscribed; bone-working is the material technique.

nodes.name: Papyrus

future.system: Construction - library (deferred-entity plan, tier B)
future.description: a library keeps portable documents and archives

nodes.auditRationale: A genuine OR route to building.library (an alternative to the scripts and paper). Paper is independent of papyrus, so no dependent is missing.

prereqAssessment.why: Papyrus sheets are laid, crossed pith strips pressed together; the plant-fibre laying and weaving craft is the technique.

nodes.name: Sexagesimal place-value
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisite exact (Mesopotamian invention). Kept; administrative-reach effect distinct from its sibling's tax-assessment effect.

prereqAssessment.why: Place-value numerals are a written notation; they arise inside Ur III cuneiform accounting.

nodes.effectRationale: Ur III scribes computed rations, labour-days and quotas for whole provinces in place-value tables: written calculation lets the centre administer further away.

nodes.name: Babylonian arithmetic
nodes.auditRationale: Kept. Feeds abacus and astronomy_records. Tax-assessment role distinct from numeral_sexagesimal's administrative reach.

prereqAssessment.why: Reciprocal tables and quadratic algorithms run on base-60 place value.

nodes.effectRationale: Field-area and expected-yield computations (the node's 'tax assessment') let levies track what land actually produces.

nodes.name: Land surveying
nodes.prereq: cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script OR mesoamerican_script
nodes.auditRationale: OR over scripts is right (rope-stretching is older than writing, but the register and assessment are not). Kept; effect is construction layout, the role its eleven dependents rely on.

prereqAssessment.why: A land register and area-based tax need written records; any of the four scripts serves (regional paths).
A land register and area-based tax need written records; any of the four scripts serves (regional paths).

A land register and area-based tax need written records; any of the four scripts serves (regional paths). Dated after surveying but an OR alternative, not must-held.

nodes.effectRationale: Measured alignments and levels (rope-stretchers, the 3-4-5 triangle) cut wasted earthwork; surveying is the gate to paved roads, aqueducts, canals and railways.

nodes.name: Square sail
nodes.auditRationale: Live unlock of coastal shipping plus the upstream-sailing effect on river haulage.

prereqAssessment.why: A hull to carry the mast; OR with raft is right because H3 seagoing craft were reed-bundle boats, not dugouts.
Reed-bundle and raft hulls carried the earliest sails (As-Sabiyah); the OR keeps both lineages.
A sail is woven cloth of sail size; the loom is the material precondition, so AND with the hull group is right.

nodes.name: Plank-built boat

future.system: Construction - harbour (deferred-entity plan, tier B)
future.description: a harbour berths plank-built cargo vessels for sea-going trade

nodes.auditRationale: Live unlock of the harbour (with stone_dry); no operand needed beyond it.

prereqAssessment.why: Plank boats grew from extended dugouts (strakes added to a dugout base).
Planks are split, adzed and fitted with copper tools (Khufu ship, Abydos boats).

nodes.name: Horse domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: DOM2 horses were domesticated by Pontic-Caspian cattle herders.

nodes.name: Donkey domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: East African cattle pastoralists domesticated the wild ass.

nodes.name: Camel domestication
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Herding know-how; Arabian and Bactrian pastoralists.

nodes.name: Spoked wheel

future.system: Battle Layer - chariots
future.description: the light, fast spoked-wheel vehicle makes the war chariot possible

future.system: freight-time consumer (ADR-032 section 7 design intent: delivery delay, carriage term, route tonnage caps)
future.description: light fast vehicles shorten overland transit once a system consumes travel time

nodes.auditRationale: Speed is the causal difference from the solid wheel.

prereqAssessment.why: The spoked wheel refines the wheel and axle.
Proxy for the bronze chisels and gouges needed to cut mortised hubs and bent felloes; weak but no better tools atom exists.

nodes.name: Chariot
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: chariotry is superseded by cavalry rather than leading into it. Effect is the chariot elite as a specialist class.

prereqAssessment.why: Light spoked wheels are what make the war chariot possible (Sintashta).
Draught horses pull it.

nodes.effectRationale: The chariot is an expensive platform crewed by a trained warrior elite (the maryannu): a specialist class the surplus must support.

nodes.name: Composite bow
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf (unit.horse_archers requires it). Herder effect is the steppe pastoral role; the A1 sling has the same operand in another Age and role.

prereqAssessment.why: Lamination refines the self bow.
Horn belly from domestic caprines.
Sinew backing and hide glue.

nodes.effectRationale: A short bow usable from horseback lets mounted herders guard and work larger herds on open steppe.

nodes.name: Fired brick
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Firing at kiln temperature.
Moulded standard bricks.

nodes.effectRationale: Kiln-fired, waterproof brick: drains and sewers unlocked, and buildings stand far longer.

nodes.name: Glaze and faience
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Glaze vitrifies only at kiln temperatures.
Alkali flux (natron, plant ash, salts) is the glass-forming ingredient.

nodes.effectRationale: A vitreous coat seals porous ceramic: glazed jars keep stored food and oil from seeping and spoiling.

nodes.name: Core-formed glass
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Glass proper follows faience and glaze.

nodes.effectRationale: Core-formed vessels are palace-workshop products: glassmaking supports another specialist artisan class.

nodes.name: Standardised weights
nodes.prereq: token_counting AND (proto_writing OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script)
nodes.auditRationale: AND/OR correct (counting tradition AND some written authority). Kept; market-integration effect.

prereqAssessment.why: Standard units descend from token accounting of measured quantities.
State-issued standards are recorded and enforced in writing; any early script path suffices. Uruk proto-writing covers Mesopotamia, so a separate cuneiform atom is unnecessary.
State-issued standards are recorded and enforced in writing; any early script path suffices.
State-issued standards are recorded and enforced in writing; any early script path suffices. Later than the Indus/Mesopotamian date but an OR alternative.

nodes.effectRationale: Trusted weights make exchange between markets quick and undisputed, so trade closes price gaps faster.

nodes.name: Civil solar calendar
nodes.prereq: calendar_lunar AND (cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script OR mesoamerican_script)
nodes.auditRationale: Kept. Effect is yield per area (scheduling), distinct from calendar_lunar's variance effect and from the water clock.

prereqAssessment.why: Month counting precedes the fixed administrative year.
An administrative year exists to date documents; any script.
Egypt's 365-day civil year is the type case.
OR alternative (regional path).
OR alternative (the Maya haab' is a 365-day civil year).

nodes.effectRationale: A fixed year anchored to the Sothic rising lets sowing be scheduled to the flood: more grain per field.

nodes.name: Water clock
nodes.auditRationale: Kept; feeds escapement_verge. Dispute-settling role chosen because it is the clepsydra's documented civil use.

prereqAssessment.why: The clepsydra is a pierced ceramic (later stone) vessel.
Hours subdivide an administered day; the Karnak clock belongs to temple timekeeping.

nodes.effectRationale: An impartial timer settles turns: water shares for irrigation (the Persian fenjan sinking bowl for qanat turns) and timed speeches in court.

nodes.name: Medical texts
nodes.prereq: herbal_remedies AND (cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script)
nodes.auditRationale: Add herbal_remedies: the earliest medical texts are mostly plant prescriptions (the Sumerian tablet, Ebers papyrus); what they write down is herbal lore. Script OR kept.

prereqAssessment.why: Sumerian prescriptions (OR).
Edwin Smith and Ebers papyri (OR).
Chinese medical writing (OR).

nodes.effectRationale: Recorded prescriptions and case descriptions spread effective treatment beyond one healer's lifetime.

nodes.name: Beekeeping
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Leaf is acceptable; beeswax for lost-wax casting is a materials link left to that lane.

prereqAssessment.why: Egyptian and Tel Rehov hives are clay cylinders.

nodes.name: Bloomery iron
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. copper_smelting (the smelting principle) is not added: the A4 sweep already requires all of A2, so the edge would be redundant.

prereqAssessment.why: Bloomery reduction runs on charcoal.
Shaft furnace temperature and atmosphere control.

nodes.effectRationale: Landmark: ore is everywhere, so iron hoes, ploughshares and axes reach ordinary farmers; equipped workers gain much more from tools.

nodes.name: Bellows
nodes.auditRationale: Its own emerged date (~1,500 BCE, Rekhmire tomb) lies inside the A3 window (~3,500-1,200 BCE), so the A4 label contradicts the dating. Moving it fills the empty A3 energy cohort. Prerequisites (A1, A2) and dependents (cast_iron A5, blast_furnace_water A6) stay order-safe.

prereqAssessment.why: Pot and bag bellows are leather diaphragms or bags; hide working supplies the material.
Controlled draught through a fired chamber is the furnace concept the bellows intensifies.

nodes.effectRationale: A forced-draught forge lets the village smith re-draw, re-temper and mend edges; tools in use wear out more slowly.

nodes.name: Carburized steel
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Carburizing works on wrought iron.

nodes.effectRationale: Carbon-hardened edges outlast soft wrought iron: tools need replacing less often.

nodes.name: Quench hardening
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Only carburized steel hardens on quenching.

nodes.effectRationale: Martensite-hard picks, wedges and axe edges cut rock and timber faster.

nodes.name: Tempering
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Tempering relieves quench brittleness.

nodes.effectRationale: Tough and hard: tempered tools neither chip nor bend, so they last and work better.

nodes.name: Wootz crucible steel
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisites are the knowledge actually needed; keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Sealed refractory crucibles fired at high temperature.
Carbon absorption principle.

nodes.effectRationale: Compact, high-value crucible-steel ingots were a staple of long-distance trade (South India to Persia and Syria).

nodes.name: Pattern welding
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf. Effect stated as the economic side of forge-welding (steeled tools), not the sword.

prereqAssessment.why: Laminates steel with iron.

nodes.effectRationale: Forge-welding a steel edge onto a soft iron body (piling, steeling) makes economical edged tools from small, uneven blooms.

nodes.name: Consonantal alphabet
nodes.auditRationale: Drop chinese_script from the OR: the alphabet derives from Egyptian hieroglyphs via Proto-Sinaitic, with cuneiform as the parallel Levantine scribal tradition. A Chinese-script player loses nothing reachable: both remaining atoms are A3 and the A5 sweep requires them anyway.

prereqAssessment.why: The Ugaritic alphabet is written in cuneiform signs; Levantine scribes trained in cuneiform administered the alphabet's world.
Proto-Sinaitic signs are acrophonic adaptations of Egyptian hieroglyphs (Serabit el-Khadim, ~1,800 BCE).
No path from the Chinese logographic system to a consonantal alphabet exists; East Asia never produced an abjad from it. The OR branch is a gameplay shortcut, not a derivation.

nodes.name: Alphabet with vowels
nodes.auditRationale: Correct derivation. Its dependents (philosophical_schools, public_theatre, state_gazette) are civic, so the effect is on Civics Points.

prereqAssessment.why: The Greek alphabet is the Phoenician abjad with consonant signs reassigned to vowels (~800 BCE).

nodes.name: Brahmi script
nodes.auditRationale: Prerequisite reflects the mainstream derivation. Effect captures its first and best-attested use: public edicts.

prereqAssessment.why: The majority view derives Brahmi from Aramaic (an abjad) with added vowel diacritics; the alternative independent origin is noted in desc.

nodes.name: Weighed silver
nodes.auditRationale: Correct prerequisites. Placed in the communication lane with money; effect is exchange efficiency.

prereqAssessment.why: Silver money is silver by weight; the shekel standard is the measure.
Cupellation yields refined silver of reliable fineness, which is what makes cut silver acceptable by weight.

nodes.name: Coinage
nodes.auditRationale: Correct prerequisites. Mint is live; coin taxation and market exchange are its two documented consequences.

prereqAssessment.why: Coins are weighed silver (or electrum) whose weight is guaranteed in advance; hacksilver is the money they replace.
A coin is a metal blank struck with an authenticating stamp; the die is a seal.

nodes.name: Cavalry
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. The classic role of light cavalry is scouting and screening.

prereqAssessment.why: Riding needs the domestic horse; nothing else is binding.

nodes.effectRationale: Mounted scouts cover several times the ground of foot parties: each exploration step reaches further.

nodes.name: Saddle

future.system: Battle Layer - mounted movement
future.description: a stable seat for cavalry and long rides; formations do not move before M7

nodes.auditRationale: Keep; the bridge from cavalry to the stirrup.

prereqAssessment.why: The saddle improves riding that already exists.
Padded, stitched leather and felt.

nodes.effectRationale: A padded seat makes long days in the saddle bearable, so riders and couriers cover more kilometres per day overland.

nodes.name: Battering ram
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Cost note: 4,970 is about 2x the A4 median and 5.6x its own dependent siege_tower; the integrator's recalibration should bring it into line.

prereqAssessment.why: Assyrian rams are wheeled sheds.
Wet hides protect the roof against fire.

nodes.effectRationale: Walled towns can no longer defy the centre behind their walls, so the reach of royal authority extends (Assyrian provincial system).

nodes.name: Siege tower and ramp
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf. Effect follows the ramp, the part of the capability with a civil use.

prereqAssessment.why: Tower and ramp complete the Assyrian assault kit that the ram began; dated two centuries after it.

nodes.effectRationale: The assault ramp is organised mass earth-moving (Lachish): the same drilled labour gangs build paths faster.

nodes.name: Ashlar fortification
nodes.auditRationale: Correct. Its live unlocks are AND/OR with other nodes (castle also needs vault_dome; lighthouse is already open via ashlar), so a reach effect gives it its own weight.

prereqAssessment.why: Cut-stone walls are ashlar work.
Laying out curtain walls, towers and gate approaches needs measured layout.

nodes.name: Crossbow
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; feeds torsion artillery and the repeating crossbow. Cost 4,180 is 1.7x the A4 median (precision casting justifies some of it).

prereqAssessment.why: A bow mounted on a stock.
The Chinese trigger is a precision bronze casting.

nodes.effectRationale: A crossbow needs little training, so town militias can shoot back: banditry and disorder cost less output.

nodes.name: Ramming warship
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; feeds state_navy.

prereqAssessment.why: A galley is a plank-built hull.
The bronze ram is cast in a closed mould.

nodes.effectRationale: A war fleet suppresses piracy on sea lanes, so bulk sea haulage needs less escort and loses fewer cargoes.

nodes.name: Qanat
nodes.auditRationale: Correct three-way AND. Deliberate leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: The mother well and access shafts are dug wells.
The gradient of a qanat (often <1:1000) needs levelling.
Underground tunnelling between shafts is mining technique.

nodes.name: Rock-cut water tunnel
nodes.auditRationale: Correct AND. Deliberate leaf; infra.aqueduct is OR with channel and arcade, so the node also carries a health effect.

prereqAssessment.why: Rock-cut tunnels are mining technique applied to water.
Eupalinos's tunnel was dug from both ends and met; surveying is essential.

nodes.name: Aqueduct channel
nodes.auditRationale: Correct AND. Feeds aqueduct_arcade.

prereqAssessment.why: A gravity channel over distance needs a measured fall.
The channel is lined and bridged in stone (Jerwan).

nodes.name: True arch
nodes.auditRationale: Keep both atoms. surveying is the weaker atom, but replacing it would add an edge without evidence.

prereqAssessment.why: The first voussoir arches are Mesopotamian mudbrick.
Laying out the curve and the centring needs measured geometry; marginal but defensible.

nodes.name: Systematic astronomical records

Alternative path: Chinese court astronomy records eclipses and comets.
Alternative path: Maya eclipse and Venus tables.

nodes.name: Intercalated calendar
nodes.auditRationale: Kept. Same operand as calendar_lunar, but a different Age and a smaller delta (the residual drift it removes).

prereqAssessment.why: The 19-year Metonic rule was derived from long observation series.

nodes.effectRationale: Leap months inserted by rule keep named months in step with the seasons, so sowing dates no longer drift.

nodes.name: Practical geometry
nodes.auditRationale: The script clause is identical to the one surveying already carries, so removing it changes no closure and no route; it only removes noise. Effect: storage geometry.

prereqAssessment.why: Area and volume rules grew out of field measurement.
Duplicate: surveying already requires exactly this OR-set (cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script OR mesoamerican_script).
Duplicate of surveying's script clause.
