prereqAssessment.why: Merchant courts apply systematic contract law, whether Islamic fiqh or the European law merchant.
There must be long-distance trade between strangers for a merchant law to govern.

nodes.effectRationale: Enforceable contracts between strangers let merchants act on distant price differences, so prices converge faster.

nodes.name: Representative assembly
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: The assembly meets to consent to taxation.
Chartered towns send representatives (OR).
Holders of land for service form the noble estate (OR).

nodes.effectRationale: Taxes granted by the estates are collected with less resistance: consent raises what the levy yields.

nodes.name: Feudal monarchy
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Fiefs held for service are the defining institution.
Monarchic succession by rule...
...or by anointed sacral kingship (Carolingian and Capetian anointing).

nodes.effectRationale: Vassals govern their fiefs for the crown, so royal authority reaches distant land without salaried officials.

nodes.name: Mercantile republic
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Merchant courts and law are the republic's base.
Venice's doge and councils were elected...
...the Hanse cities governed by charter. OR is right.

nodes.effectRationale: State-run convoys, fondachi and consulates (Venetian mude) lower the cost of moving bulk goods.

nodes.name: Military rule
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Mamluk rule rested on a standing slave army...
...the Kamakura shogunate on vassals holding land for service. OR is right.

nodes.effectRationale: Martial order suppresses disorder quickly, so unrest disrupts less output (at no grievance relief).

nodes.name: Bill of rights
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Rights enforceable in court require a developed body of law.
Parliament imposed the 1689 bill (OR).
The barons imposed Magna Carta (OR).

nodes.effectRationale: Rights the ruler cannot override, enforceable in court, remove the main causes of grievance against the state.

nodes.name: Central banking
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; the bridge is supplied by new A9 nodes (deposit_insurance, demand_management, managed_exchange_rates, microfinance) rather than a new edge.

prereqAssessment.why: The Bank of England was founded as a joint-stock company.
Note issue is the central bank's defining instrument.

nodes.effectRationale: A public bank discounts bills and settles accounts in its notes, so payment between distant markets clears faster.

nodes.name: Professional police
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. It was a leaf; this group adds penitentiary_reform (A8), road_traffic_regulation and anti_corruption_agency (A9) as successors.

prereqAssessment.why: A police force is a salaried public office.
Police enforce written law.

nodes.effectRationale: A standing civil police contains disorder before it stops work and trade.

nodes.name: Compulsory education
nodes.auditRationale: Correct pair of atoms; now also feeds school_meals and vocational_training.

prereqAssessment.why: Compulsion requires enumerating the children who must attend.
Mass schooling depends on cheap printed primers and catechisms.

nodes.effectRationale: Universal literacy lets children of labourers qualify for clerical and skilled posts, so promotion between classes runs faster.

nodes.name: Law of nations
nodes.auditRationale: Hub: four dependents across diplomacy and empire.

prereqAssessment.why: The law of nations systematises treaty practice.
Grotius built on Roman ius gentium and natural law; a jurist tradition is a must-hold.

nodes.effectRationale: Neutral rights and freedom of the seas (Mare Liberum, 1609) protect neutral shipping, cutting the risk cost of bulk haulage.

nodes.name: Statistical office
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Regular tables extend the census into continuous counts.
Tabulation needs positional arithmetic (OR).
Rod arithmetic is the East Asian route (OR).

nodes.effectRationale: Known numbers of mouths by parish let stores and relief be sized to need, so granaries relieve famine more.

nodes.name: Boards of health
nodes.auditRationale: Key public-health root; feeds environmental_regulation and the new public-health lane.

prereqAssessment.why: Health magistrates counted the sick and the dead to decide quarantine and closure.
Airs-and-waters (miasma) medicine supplied the rationale for sanitation and isolation.

nodes.effectRationale: Quarantine and sanitary powers cut deaths from plague and fever in all age groups.

nodes.name: Resident embassies
nodes.auditRationale: Gap A3 to A7 is bridged by the new safe_conduct and merchant_consuls (A6); no edge added because resident_embassies is runtime and the bridge is historical precedent, not a must-hold.

prereqAssessment.why: Resident ambassadors manage standing treaty relations.
A salaried envoy kept abroad for years is an appointed office of state.

nodes.effectRationale: Standing channels settle disputes before they turn into raids and war scares, so disorder costs less output.

nodes.name: Separation of powers
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Montesquieu (1748) predates 1787 but the written_constitution node dates from 1653, so the order holds.

prereqAssessment.why: The separation is laid down by a constitution.

nodes.effectRationale: Credible commitment (North and Weingast): when the executive cannot seize or repudiate at will, taxpayers and lenders pay more willingly.

nodes.name: Written constitution
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; nine dependents.

prereqAssessment.why: A fundamental law is drafted in the vocabulary of systematic law.
Constitutions were made by representative conventions.

nodes.effectRationale: One fundamental law fixes the organs of government for every province alike: authority carries further with less negotiation.

nodes.name: Absolute monarchy
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). divine_right is the theory behind European absolutism, but adding it would exclude non-European absolutisms and Bodin-style sovereignty theory; kept as is.

prereqAssessment.why: Absolutism rested on a standing army independent of the estates.
Intendants and governors...
...or an examination bureaucracy (Qing). OR is right.

nodes.effectRationale: Taxes levied without the estates' consent (the taille, the poll tax of Peter I) let the crown extract more of the output: a landmark fiscal effect.

nodes.name: Constitutional monarchy
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). The nested OR captures the unwritten English route; sound.

prereqAssessment.why: The monarchy remains hereditary by rule.
Bound by a constitution...
...or, as in England 1689, by a bill of rights...
...together with a parliament.

nodes.effectRationale: Parliament's control of the purse makes taxes credible and accepted after 1689 (higher extraction), and petitions to it relieve grievance. Two smaller effects distinguish it from absolute_monarchy's single fiscal effect.

nodes.name: Federation
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: A federal compact must be written.
Member units are self-governing towns or cantons...
...or provinces/states. OR is right.

nodes.effectRationale: Member states govern their own territory under the union, so the polity's effective reach extends further.

nodes.name: Presidential republic
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: A separately elected executive is the separation of powers in practice.
The presidency is an elected magistracy.

nodes.effectRationale: A fixed-term executive cannot be toppled by shifting majorities, so political crises disrupt output less.

nodes.name: Abolition of slavery and serfdom
nodes.auditRationale: Landmark leaf; its weak prerequisite is reported as a finding rather than changed, because the emerged text dates a precursor to 594 BCE.

prereqAssessment.why: Abolition is an act of law dissolving a legal status, so systematic law is needed. The single A4 atom under-specifies the A8 node (see findings), but the obvious extra atom (social_contract, 1651) would be dated after the node's Solonian precursor (594 BCE), so it is not proposed until the emerged text is narrowed.

nodes.effectRationale: Freed slaves and serfs may leave the land they were bound to, so people move far more freely.

civ7.analog: Serfdom (Russia unique civic; Krestyanskaya Reforma tradition)

nodes.name: General staff
nodes.auditRationale: Runtime anchor; feeds integrated_alliance_command and nuclear_deterrence, and the new military_railways, military_intelligence, motorized_supply, defence_research_agencies and independent_air_arm.

prereqAssessment.why: A staff plans for a permanent army.
Staff work is map work; the Prussian staff's topographical section is central. cartography (A5) is the generic map-making atom.

nodes.effectRationale: Staff reconnaissance and survey maps let formations see further than their own pickets.

nodes.name: Laws of war conventions
nodes.auditRationale: Extension of law_of_nations (novelty 0.5 in the rubric); feeds collective_security and international_tribunals.

prereqAssessment.why: Geneva and Hague conventions extend the law of nations; a single atom is right for an extension.

nodes.effectRationale: Protection of the wounded, prisoners and civilians and the Red Cross medical service lower deaths among those caught in war.

nodes.name: Mass political parties
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Mass parties organize a mass electorate.
Party newspapers and pamphlets; mass_press (A8) would be closer but is in another lane and not needed for the closure.

nodes.effectRationale: Party machines and workers' parties carry men of modest origin into councils and office: faster social promotion.

nodes.name: Mass suffrage
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Its desc says 'by secret ballot', which overlaps secret_ballot; suggest dropping that phrase from the desc.

prereqAssessment.why: The franchise elects a representative chamber.
Voters are drawn from a public register of adults.

nodes.effectRationale: Every adult has a lawful voice: grievances go to the polls. Landmark of the lane, hence 0.04.

nodes.name: Responsible ministers
nodes.auditRationale: Keep.

prereqAssessment.why: Ministers answer to the elected chamber.
Ministers head departments of appointed officials.

nodes.effectRationale: Ministers answerable in the chamber for every act of their departments discipline officials everywhere.

nodes.name: Universal conscription
nodes.auditRationale: Runtime anchor; feeds total_mobilization and the new army_reserves and veterans_benefits.

prereqAssessment.why: Conscription fills a permanent army.
Registration of the age class needs a count of persons; the Jourdan Law worked from municipal registers.

nodes.effectRationale: Service teaches peasant conscripts literacy, drill and trades and takes them to towns, speeding movement into specialist classes.

nodes.name: Parliamentary government
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Single prerequisite is the defining one.

prereqAssessment.why: Cabinet government is ministerial responsibility made routine; it already requires representative_assembly.

nodes.effectRationale: Budgets voted by the elected house and spent by ministers it controls were accepted and paid (nineteenth-century Britain), raising extraction.

nodes.name: Central economic planning
nodes.auditRationale: Correct atoms; feeds marxist_leninist_state.

prereqAssessment.why: A plan is written against statistical balances of output and stocks.
Central allocation needs fast reporting from and instructions to distant enterprises.

nodes.effectRationale: State procurement at plan prices captures a larger share of output for the centre.

nodes.name: Marxist–Leninist state
nodes.auditRationale: Missing bridge: socialism (A8 ideology) has no dependents, and central_planning requires only official_statistics and telegraph, so today a polity can found a Marxist-Leninist state without the socialist ideology it embodies. Adding socialism (dated 1825-1848, before 1922) closes the ideology-to-regime link, as fascism does for fascist_state. Note for the integrator: socialism is a D13 civic, so this edge lands only when D13 is imported.

prereqAssessment.why: The party-state is a mass party in power.
The planned economy defines it.

nodes.effectRationale: Five-Year Plans gave coal, ore and timber extraction first claim on labour and investment, so extractors produce more.

nodes.name: One-party state
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: The single party is a mass party.
Constitutionally entrenched (USSR 1924)...
...or held by force (Kemalist Turkey). OR is right.

nodes.effectRationale: Party cells in every district and workplace carry central orders down, extending administrative reach.

nodes.name: Gift exchange networks
nodes.auditRationale: Leaf in the index; bridged by new nodes craft_specialists and barter_exchange (and C1's prestige_leadership).

prereqAssessment.why: Exchange partnerships are negotiated between kin groups; the council is the band's earliest institution.

nodes.effectRationale: Rare stone and shell move hand to hand between bands, so scarce goods reach places that lack them.

civ7.analog: Cah-nah-ha (Mississippian unique civic; Gift Economy tradition)

nodes.name: Oral tradition
nodes.auditRationale: Root of the lane; no prerequisite is right for the earliest transmissible lore. Its single dependent (communal_feasts) plus the new A1-A3 arts/learning nodes now hang from it.
nodes.effectRationale: Remembered lore of famine foods, water holes and fallback grounds is what lets a band ride out a bad season; the effect is on the household's absorbable shortfall, not on output.

nodes.name: Ritual specialists
nodes.auditRationale: A1 belief root. Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Ochre is the oldest ritual pigment (Blombos, Qafzeh burials).

nodes.effectRationale: Ritual specialists were also the band's healers, holding knowledge of medicinal plants (ethnographic shamans), so baseline mortality falls slightly.

nodes.name: War bands
nodes.auditRationale: A1 root of the military lane; feeds citizen_militia, steppe_empire and the new village_defences and chiefly_retinue.

prereqAssessment.why: The raid leader is chosen by the kin heads.
Projectile weapons (Jebel Sahaba victims carry microlith points); OR with atlatl is right.
Alternative projectile technology; OR with bow_simple.

nodes.effectRationale: An armed party can push through neighbours' land that an unarmed group would avoid, so each Explore step reaches further.

nodes.name: Ancestor veneration
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; this tranche gives it two dependents (first_settler_rights, segmentary_lineage), so no prerequisite change is needed.

prereqAssessment.why: Rites for the dead extend the ritual repertoire.
Settled farming households keep their dead in the house...
...or herding lineages; OR mirrors hereditary_rank.

nodes.effectRationale: Houses that hold the ancestors are rebuilt and maintained on the same spot for generations (Çatalhöyük house sequences), so dwellings last longer.

nodes.name: Communal feasts
nodes.auditRationale: Causally sound; Natufian and Göbekli Tepe feasting predates full domestication, which the early cereal_cultivation atom respects.

prereqAssessment.why: Feasts mark a remembered calendar and recite genealogies; the lore is the frame of the event.
Pre-domestication cultivation (~11,500 BCE) supplies the storable surplus that big feasts consume; dated before Hilazon Tachtit.
A herd is the alternative feast surplus; OR is correct since either route suffices.

nodes.effectRationale: Shared feasts settle tension between households (grievance) and draw contributions and guests from a wider territory around the host settlement (catchment).

nodes.name: Court patronage
nodes.auditRationale: Correct OR of the two Bronze Age patrons. Dependents arts_academies and public_opera are long jumps (A3 to A7) but they are genuine lineages of patronage, not gaps.

prereqAssessment.why: Temple estates fed full-time craftsmen in Uruk before kings did.
Divine kings commissioned royal workshops (Old Kingdom); an alternative route, so OR.

nodes.effectRationale: Rulers and temples feed workshops of full-time sculptors, goldsmiths and builders, enlarging the specialist share a society can carry.

nodes.name: Customs and tolls
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. This group adds internal_toll_abolition (A8) as a further successor.

prereqAssessment.why: Customs are a levy.
There must be trade flows to tax.

nodes.effectRationale: Duties at gates, fords and borders capture a share of trade that a levy on the harvest misses.

nodes.name: Debt remission edicts
nodes.auditRationale: A deliberate leaf: the crisis edict is superseded by standing institutions (interest_bearing_credit regulation, poor relief).

prereqAssessment.why: Remission edicts (misharum) are royal legal acts cancelling written obligations.
Remission is proclaimed by a king acting as guarantor of justice at accession.

nodes.effectRationale: Periodic cancellation of debts frees debt-bondsmen and stops grievance from piling up.

nodes.name: Dynastic marriage
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: succession claims are handled in legitimacy-succession; nothing downstream must hold it.

prereqAssessment.why: There must be a royal house whose rank passes by descent.
Marriage seals an alliance between houses as it did between communities.

nodes.effectRationale: Marriage ties between royal houses end border raiding between them, so less output is lost to disorder.

nodes.name: Family and inheritance law
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. It was a leaf; this group adds married_womens_property (A8) as its successor.

prereqAssessment.why: Family law is a chapter of written law.

nodes.effectRationale: Written duties of support, guardianship and adoption put orphans and widows' children under someone's care when food is short.

nodes.name: Planned towns
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds building_regulation.

prereqAssessment.why: A plan laid out before building needs officials to survey and enforce it.
Harappan grids and drains are built in standard fired brick.

nodes.effectRationale: Regular plots and drains let houses stand wall to wall, so more people live in each block.

nodes.name: Royal archives
nodes.auditRationale: Sound. stamp_seal is a minor atom but causally present (sealed archives); no change proposed.

prereqAssessment.why: An archive needs trained scribes to write, file and read it.
Sealed tablets and bullae authenticate the filed record; weak but historically present at Ebla and Mari. Kept: not worth a change.

nodes.effectRationale: Filed accounts, treaties and precedents let the palace govern distant places from records instead of personal memory: administrative reach extends.

nodes.name: Scribal schools
nodes.prereq: cuneiform OR hieroglyphic OR chinese_script OR mesoamerican_script
nodes.auditRationale: Any one script suffices, so OR is right. Gate of the learning lane with two dependents.

prereqAssessment.why: Edubba schools of Sumer taught cuneiform.
Egyptian scribal training is an independent route.
Shang-Zhou scribal training; independent route.
Maya scribes trained in their script; independent route.

nodes.effectRationale: Schools are a route by which sons of farmers and craftsmen enter the literate class (promotion); trained accountant-scribes collect dues more completely (tax).

nodes.name: Temple households
nodes.auditRationale: Sound; now also feeds temple_almsgiving.

prereqAssessment.why: Priests manage the estates.
Uruk temple accounts grew out of token counting.

nodes.effectRationale: Temple storehouses kept grain under audited accounts for redistribution, so granaries hold more years of demand.

nodes.name: Trade treaties
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now bridged by the new merchant_consuls (A6).

prereqAssessment.why: A trade treaty is a sworn treaty with commercial clauses.
There must be a merchant network to protect (Assur-Kanesh).

nodes.effectRationale: Guaranteed safety and fixed tolls let merchants bring stocks to foreign markets sooner.

civ7.analog: Code of Laws (Improve Trade Relations action)

nodes.name: Water rights
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now feeds water_turn_shares and water_boards.

prereqAssessment.why: There must be canals to allocate.
Water shares and bank-maintenance duties are written law (Hammurabi 53-56).

nodes.effectRationale: Maintained banks and fixed water turns keep fields watered in dry years, so harvests swing less.

nodes.name: Citizen militia
nodes.auditRationale: Feeds revolutionary_republic; distinct from standing_army (unpaid, part-time citizens).

prereqAssessment.why: The militia is the armed body of the community.
Hoplite service and the assembly of arms-bearers go together; OR with elite_council is right.
Oligarchic poleis also fielded citizen hoplites; OR branch.

nodes.effectRationale: A citizen army defends the city's whole territory (chora), so outlying fields can be worked.

nodes.name: Daughter colonies
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: later colonization forms (veteran_colonies, settler_charters) rest on land administration, not on overseas apoikiai.

prereqAssessment.why: Overseas founding needs sailing ships.
The colony is bound to its mother city by oath, cult and kinship.

nodes.effectRationale: The mother city organises and equips a large founding party under an oikist.

nodes.name: Conditional mandate
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; it now feeds state_orthodoxy (Han Confucian orthodoxy).

prereqAssessment.why: The Mandate reworks sacral kingship into a conditional grant.
Virtue and tyranny are judged against written norms.

nodes.effectRationale: A ruler whose mandate depends on the people's welfare is bound to relieve famine; Chinese state granaries were justified this way, so granaries relieve famine more.

nodes.name: Public games
nodes.auditRationale: Sound religious-festival lineage. Dependents professional_sport and public_theatre are kept (see public_theatre note).

prereqAssessment.why: Olympia began as a sanctuary festival with feasting; games are the formalized descendant.
Games were held at sanctuaries under priestly calendars and truces.

nodes.effectRationale: Regular contests channel rivalry and young men's violence into licensed spectacle, so unrest costs less output.

nodes.name: Royal post
nodes.auditRationale: Sound. A road atom would be defensible but the Achaemenid post ran on existing tracks; not added.

prereqAssessment.why: Relay stations are staffed and provisioned by officials.
Mounted relays are what makes a post faster than a runner.

nodes.effectRationale: Orders and reports cross the realm in days instead of weeks, so the centre's authority decays far more slowly with distance; the lane's Iron Age landmark, hence 0.05.

civ7.analog: Satrapies (Čāpār-Kāna tradition, Achaemenid Persia unique civic)

nodes.name: Scriptural canon
nodes.prereq: organized_priesthood AND (abjad OR alphabet_vowels OR brahmi OR chinese_script)
nodes.auditRationale: Four dependents. The oral Rigveda in emerged sits awkwardly with the script prerequisite; the capability (a fixed text studied by clergy) is right, so the edge is kept and the emerged note should say the Vedic canon was fixed orally.

prereqAssessment.why: A trained clergy fixes and studies the canon.
Torah redaction; the script OR is right...
...Greek-script canons...
...Indic canons (the Rigveda itself was oral, so its ~1,200 BCE date is a compilation date, not a written one)...
...Chinese classics.

nodes.effectRationale: A body of texts studied by a trained clergy creates the first institution of textual scholarship, so civic learning accumulates faster.

nodes.name: State navy
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now bridged by the new coaling_stations (A8).

prereqAssessment.why: The purpose-built warship is the fleet's material basis.
A permanent fleet is paid from revenue (Athenian trierarchy and silver).

nodes.effectRationale: A permanent fleet suppresses piracy on the grain routes, lowering the cost of bulk haulage.

nodes.name: Building regulation
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds zoning, fire_brigades and housing_acts.

prereqAssessment.why: Imperial building rules are statutes of systematic law.
Regulation of height and fire breaks extends town planning.

nodes.effectRationale: Limits on height, required materials and fire breaks mean fewer houses collapse or burn.

nodes.name: Legal profession
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. It was a leaf; this group adds roman_law_revival (A6) and legal_aid (A9) as successors.

prereqAssessment.why: Jurists comment on and develop a systematic law.

nodes.effectRationale: Jurists' opinions refine contract and sale law, so merchants can rely on agreements made far away.

nodes.name: Jury courts
nodes.auditRationale: Keep as a deliberate leaf: later courts in this group descend from royal and appellate justice, not from the jury.

prereqAssessment.why: Juries are panels of the citizen body.
Juries apply written law.

nodes.effectRationale: Judgment by one's peers is accepted where an official's verdict would be resented.

nodes.name: Mercenary contracts
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now feeds the new colonial_regiments.

prereqAssessment.why: Hire for pay presupposes wages counted in coin (the Ten Thousand were paid in darics).

nodes.effectRationale: Soldiers of fortune travel very long distances for pay and often settle where discharged.

nodes.name: Missionary religion
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now feeds missionary_societies (A8).

prereqAssessment.why: Missions carry a fixed teaching.
Ashoka sent missions as embassies; Paul travelled the diplomatic road network.

nodes.effectRationale: Missionaries and pilgrims returned with accounts of far lands (Faxian, Xuanzang), so exploration reaches further.

nodes.name: Monastic orders
nodes.auditRationale: Sound; now also feeds mendicant_orders.

prereqAssessment.why: Monastic rules organize study of the canon.

nodes.effectRationale: Monastic estates with a disciplined labour force and a long horizon drained, manured and improved land, so land yields more.

nodes.name: Philosophical schools
nodes.prereq: scribal_schools AND (abjad OR alphabet_vowels OR brahmi OR chinese_script)
nodes.auditRationale: Sound; four dependents. RP is deliberately not used here (the RP coefficient is oversubscribed across tranche 2).

prereqAssessment.why: Lasting schools presuppose a literate teaching tradition.
Script routes: Hebrew/Aramaic wisdom schools.
Greek Academy and Lyceum.
Indian darshana schools; Brahmi is ~300 BCE, later than the Buddha but in the OR group only.
Confucian and Mohist schools.

nodes.effectRationale: A school with a succession of heads, a curriculum and a library is the institutional template every later academy and university copies; they reach maturity faster.

nodes.name: Political philosophy
nodes.auditRationale: Sound; three dependents.

prereqAssessment.why: Political theory is a branch of the schools' argument.
Comparing constitutions presupposes written law to compare.

nodes.effectRationale: Systematic thought about just rule raises the rate at which a society produces civic ideas; one of the few CP coefficients in this group.

nodes.name: Public granaries
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds alimenta and price_support.

prereqAssessment.why: Officials buy, store and release the stock.
The granary is filled from grain levies.

nodes.effectRationale: State stocks released in dearth relieve famine more than private stores can.

nodes.name: Public theatre
nodes.auditRationale: Kept with the note on public_games; no change is worth the churn.

prereqAssessment.why: Weak causally (drama grew from the Dionysia, a religious festival, not athletic games), but public_games carries the festival-crowd institution and the same parents (communal_feasts AND organized_priesthood); replacing it would only duplicate that closure.
Written Greek drama.
Sanskrit drama and the Natyashastra.

nodes.effectRationale: Drama before the citizen body airs and works through public quarrels (comedy mocks the powerful, tragedy rehearses civic dilemmas): grievance builds more slowly.

nodes.name: State academy
nodes.auditRationale: Sound; dependent research_university.

prereqAssessment.why: The Mouseion and the Han Taixue institutionalize existing schools of learning.
A state library grows out of palace archives.

nodes.effectRationale: A state school recruits talent into office (promotion) and turns out officials trained in one canon, extending administrative reach.

civ7.analog: Zhi (Xiu Taixue tradition, Han unique civic)

nodes.name: State gazette
nodes.auditRationale: Leaf by design: the official-news genre's modern descendants enter through printing and the press (printed_newspapers, mass_press), which do not need it.

prereqAssessment.why: The gazette travels by the official post.
Acta Diurna in Latin.
Han-Tang court gazettes (dibao).

nodes.effectRationale: Published decrees reach officials and townsmen in one authoritative form: fewer rumours turning into disorder, and provincial officials act on the same orders.

nodes.name: State monopolies
nodes.auditRationale: Keep as a deliberate leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: Monopolies are run by salaried officials.
Salt was the first staple monopolized.

nodes.effectRationale: State salt works and iron foundries concentrate capital and labour at scale (Han monopoly): extraction yields more per worker.

nodes.name: State religion
nodes.auditRationale: Hub (feeds canon_law, divine_right, legal_estates and five new nodes). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: There must be a clergy to establish.
Establishment is enforced by officials.

nodes.effectRationale: An established clergy preaching obedience in every parish damps the output cost of unrest.

nodes.name: Statecraft doctrine
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: its successors are in administration-fiscal (civil_service_examinations) and do not hinge on it.

prereqAssessment.why: The Arthashastra and Han Feizi answer the philosophers' question with manuals.
The manuals are about running appointed officials.

nodes.effectRationale: Rules for supervising, rotating and spying on officials keep distant agents obedient: authority decays more slowly with distance.

nodes.name: Tributary relations
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: the tribute order is an end-state of its branch; hegemonic leagues are dated earlier and cannot depend on it.

prereqAssessment.why: Tribute missions are embassies.
A central court office (Han Office of Dependent States) receives tribute and confers titles.

nodes.effectRationale: Titles and gifts bind peripheral rulers to the court, extending reach without garrisons.

nodes.name: Steppe empire
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound three-way AND.

prereqAssessment.why: Clans are sworn to the khan.
The retinue becomes the decimal army.
Mounted archery is the military base.

nodes.effectRationale: The khan allots pastures and seasonal routes among clans and keeps the peace among them, so herds graze better land and yield more.

nodes.name: Canon law
nodes.auditRationale: After the religious_reform change it would be a leaf; it now feeds mendicant_orders, whose rule was approved under canon law.

prereqAssessment.why: Church courts need an established church.
Gratian systematized canon law on Roman-law method.

nodes.effectRationale: Canon law was a founding faculty of Bologna and Paris; a teachable law corpus makes universities mature faster.

nodes.name: Common law
nodes.auditRationale: Keep as a deliberate leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: Royal judges build on and record written law.
Royal judges are appointed officials of the crown.

nodes.effectRationale: Itinerant royal justices carry the king's law into every county: authority reaches further.

nodes.name: Elective succession
nodes.auditRationale: Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Election is a succession rule.
The electoral college is a council of magnates.

nodes.effectRationale: Electors bargain capitulations from each candidate, writing the magnates' grievances into the ruler's oath.

nodes.name: Forest law
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds nature_conservation (and T7's sustained_yield_forestry).

prereqAssessment.why: Reserved forests are defined and recorded tracts.
Forest rights were granted and policed through tenure (verderers, foresters).

nodes.effectRationale: Licensed cutting and coppice rotation keep woods productive, so loggers yield more over time.

civ7.analog: Angevin Empire (England unique civic; Charter of the Forest tradition)

nodes.name: Legal estates
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: an order of society later dissolved (abolition, civil_code) rather than built upon.

prereqAssessment.why: Orders are hereditary ranks fixed in law.
The clergy as a legal estate presupposes an established church.

nodes.effectRationale: Each order has recognised rights and an assembly voice, so conflicts are bargained out rather than fought.

nodes.name: Manorialism
nodes.auditRationale: Turn the heavy-plough requirement into an OR with systematic law (the Roman colonate binding tenants to the soil), so the manor is reachable in Mediterranean economies.

prereqAssessment.why: The bipartite manor was not a heavy-plough artefact: Byzantine, Italian and Iberian estates bound tenants (the colonate, 332 CE) while ploughing with the ard. The heavy plough should be one route, not a must-hold.
The lord holds the manor by service tenure.

nodes.effectRationale: Demesne and tenant strips are worked to a common calendar with shared teams, so land yields more.

nodes.name: Market fairs
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: fairs were superseded by permanent exchanges (stock_exchange, commodity_exchange).

prereqAssessment.why: A fair is a chartered privilege with its own peace and court.
Fairs gather long-distance merchants.

nodes.effectRationale: Periodic fairs draw stored goods to market at known dates, so stocks are sold sooner.

nodes.name: Military orders
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: a regional institution with no must-hold successor.

prereqAssessment.why: Knights live under a monastic rule.
The orders held land and castles for military service.

nodes.effectRationale: The orders were founded to guard pilgrim roads; chains of castles and hospices make long routes viable.

nodes.name: Systematic theology
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now feeds liberation_theology (A9).

prereqAssessment.why: Theology reasons about the canon.
With philosophical method.

nodes.effectRationale: Scholastic disputation and the theology faculty were the core of the medieval university's method, so universities cut research cost more.

nodes.name: Elective monarchy
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: The defining rule: an electoral college chooses the king.
The electors are magnates holding land and office for service.

nodes.effectRationale: Charters extracted at each election entrench a large privileged estate (the Polish szlachta was ~8% of the population), so a larger upper class is sustainable.

nodes.name: Arts academies
nodes.auditRationale: Sound. If public_museums takes court_patronage instead (below), arts_academies keeps dependents through the new modernist_design, arts_councils and public_art_programmes.

prereqAssessment.why: Academies were founded and chartered by princes.
The academy model and the theory of the arts are humanist.

nodes.effectRationale: Admission and prizes by competition (Prix de Rome) open the artist's career to talented commoners: faster social promotion.

nodes.name: Colonial administration
nodes.auditRationale: Hub of the empire lane (indirect_rule, settler_land_grants and five new nodes).

prereqAssessment.why: There must be overseas claims to administer.
Viceroyalties extend the provincial-governor model overseas.

nodes.effectRationale: A home council, viceroys and colonial law let the state govern territories far beyond its old reach.

nodes.name: Copyright
nodes.auditRationale: Keep as a deliberate leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: Copyright exists because printing makes copying cheap.
A property right in texts enforced in court.

nodes.effectRationale: Paid authors write more: more books, pamphlets and treatises per person.

nodes.name: Divine right of kings
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: the doctrine is superseded rather than built on (social_contract answers it).

prereqAssessment.why: Divine right is a theory of sacral kingship.
Resistance as sin presumes an established church.

nodes.effectRationale: Preaching that resistance is sin damps disorder slightly.

nodes.name: Enlightenment
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf with no dependents in the whole graph, which is wrong for the hinge of modern civic thought. Bridged in this file by public_libraries (enlightenment AND compulsory_education); integrators may also wire it into classical_liberalism or separation_of_powers in other groups.

prereqAssessment.why: The republic of letters runs on the societies' journals and correspondence.
Enlightenment critique of government is political philosophy applied.

nodes.effectRationale: Careers open to talent and reasoned reform of punishment and toleration: faster promotion and grievance building more slowly.

nodes.name: Humanism
nodes.auditRationale: Emerged (~1,350 CE) lies in the A6 window, but the movement's institutional spread is A7; Age kept (a crossing is not a reason to move).

prereqAssessment.why: Humanists recovered the classical schools' texts.
Cheap paper made the humanist book and letter culture possible before print.

nodes.effectRationale: Rhetoric and letters became the qualification for secretaries, chancellors and diplomats of lay birth: faster social promotion.

nodes.name: Mercantilism
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: a doctrine answered by free_trade, not built upon.

prereqAssessment.why: Trade rules presuppose a merchant law.
Mercantilist policy works through tariffs.

nodes.effectRationale: Tariffs and export monopolies channel trade revenue to the crown, raising what taxes extract.

nodes.name: Military academies
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: the general staff descends from staff practice, not from the academies; no must-hold successor.

prereqAssessment.why: Schools train officers for the permanent army.
Gunnery and fortification were taught from printed mathematical manuals.

nodes.effectRationale: Commissions earned by schooling rather than purchase or birth speed promotion into the officer class.

nodes.name: Poor law
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; feeds school_meals and public_works_relief.

prereqAssessment.why: The parish or town administers relief.
Relief is financed by a compulsory rate.

nodes.effectRationale: Parish relief in dearth keeps the destitute from starving.

nodes.name: Press licensing
nodes.auditRationale: Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Licensing regulates printers.
Censors and licensers are officials.

nodes.effectRationale: Seditious pamphlets are stopped before they circulate, so disorder costs less output (the cost is borne later via press_freedom).

nodes.name: Public museums
nodes.auditRationale: Replace arts_academies with court_patronage: museums are opened princely and scholarly cabinets. arts_academies keeps its new dependents in this file.

prereqAssessment.why: The first public museums (Ashmolean 1683 from the Tradescant cabinet, British Museum 1753 from Sloane, Uffizi opened 1765) grew from princely and scholarly collections, not from art academies; court_patronage is the causal input.
Collections were catalogued and studied by the learned societies (the Ashmolean housed the Oxford Philosophical Society).

nodes.effectRationale: Open collections make history and nature a public study, raising the society's civic output; sparing CP use.

nodes.name: Public opera and concerts
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; bridged by the new recorded_music_industry (radio_broadcasting AND public_opera).

prereqAssessment.why: Ticketed opera is theatre opened to a paying public.
Opera began as court spectacle (Mantua, Florence) before Venice sold tickets.

nodes.effectRationale: Cheap seats in the opera house and concert hall give townspeople a shared public pleasure: grievance builds more slowly.

nodes.name: Religious reform movements
nodes.auditRationale: The OR admitted a scripture-less route through canon_law alone, which contradicts the node's own capability (lay readers challenging clergy from the text). The new expression is the required core; no Age or tree crossing is involved.

prereqAssessment.why: Printed vernacular scripture and pamphlets carried the Reformation.

As an OR alternative it lets reform be reached without any scriptural canon (canon_law requires state_religion and legal_code_roman, not scripture). Reform movements appeal to scripture against the clergy; the established clergy is already required through scriptural_canon's organized_priesthood.
Sola scriptura: the appeal to the text is the movement's core.

nodes.effectRationale: Reading scripture for oneself drove lay literacy (Protestant schooling), so people rise between classes faster.

nodes.name: Scientific societies
nodes.auditRationale: Sound; four dependents.

prereqAssessment.why: The academies grew out of humanist sodalities.
Published proceedings (Philosophical Transactions) are the societies' product.

nodes.effectRationale: Claims tested by experiment and published to peers raise the yield of every researcher; the learning lane's early-modern landmark.

civ7.analog: Society of Antiquaries (Great Britain unique civic)

nodes.name: Social contract
nodes.auditRationale: Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Contract theory continues classical political philosophy.
Leviathan and the Two Treatises circulated in print.

nodes.effectRationale: Rule argued to rest on consent invites petitions and redress, so grievance builds more slowly.

nodes.name: State-sponsored exploration
nodes.auditRationale: Landmark node; feeds colonial_administration, chartered_companies and geographical_societies.

prereqAssessment.why: Portuguese voyages; OR with ocean_junk is right (Zheng He).
Ming fleets; OR branch.
The crown appoints and funds the commander and claims the finds.

nodes.effectRationale: Landmark: chartered state voyages push exploration much further per order and over a wider range.

nodes.name: Stock exchange
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; feeds insurance_underwriting and commodity_exchange.

prereqAssessment.why: Shares must exist before they can be traded.

nodes.effectRationale: A share market finances enterprises beyond family capital, sustaining a larger merchant and managerial class.

nodes.name: State sovereignty system
nodes.auditRationale: Feeds great_power_congress.

prereqAssessment.why: Mutual recognition is practised through permanent embassies.
Sovereign equality is a doctrine of the law of nations.

nodes.effectRationale: Recognised borders and exclusive authority at home remove rival jurisdictions, so the state's reach consolidates.

nodes.name: Antitrust law
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf of the corporate branch.

prereqAssessment.why: Trusts were combinations of limited companies.
Antitrust is legislation passed against organised interests.

nodes.effectRationale: Broken cartels stop holding prices apart between markets, and the public resentment of monopolies eases.

nodes.name: Civil code
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. It was a leaf; this group adds tenancy_protection and consumer_protection (A9).

prereqAssessment.why: The code systematizes Roman-derived law.
Codification followed the constitutional settlement in France.

nodes.effectRationale: One code for persons, property and contract replaces hundreds of local customs: trade across regions faces one law.

civ7.analog: Code Civil des Français (French Empire unique civic)

nodes.name: Liberalism
nodes.auditRationale: Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Rights theory comes from contract theory.
Free-market argument presumes enforceable commercial law.

nodes.effectRationale: Removing internal tolls, monopolies and price controls lets arbitrage close price gaps faster.

nodes.name: Conservatism
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: an ideology of defence, not a foundation others build on.

prereqAssessment.why: Conservatism is a reaction to the claim of popular sovereignty.

nodes.effectRationale: Conservative government kept unpaid local notables (justices of the peace, Landräte) in administration, extending reach cheaply.

nodes.name: Cooperatives
nodes.auditRationale: Kept; now feeds microfinance.

prereqAssessment.why: Members pool wages to buy shares in the store.

Guild mutual funds are the associational precedent; weaker than socialism (Rochdale were Owenites), but replacing it would leave craft_guilds with no dependent in its own lane, and Raiffeisen co-operatives were not socialist.

nodes.effectRationale: Co-operative stores and credit unions give members goods on credit and a dividend, so households absorb short falls in supply.

nodes.name: Customs union
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds C1's supranational_union.

prereqAssessment.why: A union abolishes internal tolls and shares an external tariff.
Members bind themselves by treaty.

nodes.effectRationale: Goods cross member borders without toll stops, so bulk haulage costs less.

nodes.name: Factory inspection
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; feeds workmens_compensation, minimum_wage and occupational_safety.

prereqAssessment.why: Inspectors are salaried officials with powers of entry.
Inspection began in power-driven textile mills (Factory Act 1833).

nodes.effectRationale: Fencing of machinery and limits on hours reduce deaths from accidents and exhaustion.

nodes.name: Free trade
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds multilateral_trade_rules.

prereqAssessment.why: Free trade is the doctrine of Smith and Ricardo put into law.
Tariffs must exist to be lowered.

nodes.effectRationale: With tariffs lowered, arbitrage between markets is no longer blocked, so price gaps close much faster.

nodes.name: Concert of powers
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now feeds the new river_commissions (the Rhine Commission was created at Vienna).

prereqAssessment.why: A concert presupposes recognised sovereign powers.

nodes.effectRationale: Congress diplomacy kept general war away for decades, so less output is lost to disorder.

nodes.name: Heritage preservation
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: an end-state protection law.

prereqAssessment.why: Listing monuments extends the museum's curatorial idea to buildings.
Inspectors of monuments are officials.

nodes.effectRationale: Listed buildings must be maintained and may not be pulled down: the building stock lasts longer.

nodes.name: Income tax
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. It was a leaf; this group adds withholding_tax, value_added_tax, executive_budget and fiscal_equalization (A9).

prereqAssessment.why: Income tax is a form of taxation.
Assessing declared incomes needs statistical administration.

nodes.effectRationale: A broad base on all incomes raises far more than levies on land and goods. Landmark of the fiscal lane, hence 0.06.

nodes.name: Indirect rule
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf: end-state of the colonial branch.

prereqAssessment.why: Indirect rule is a mode of colonial government.
Local rulers are bound by treaty (princely states' subsidiary alliances).

nodes.effectRationale: Ruling through local princes and residents extends control at little administrative cost.

nodes.name: International organizations
nodes.auditRationale: Hub with six existing dependents and several new A9 ones.

prereqAssessment.why: Permanent bodies are created by treaty under the law of nations.
The first such body (International Telegraph Union, 1865) existed to run the telegraph.

nodes.effectRationale: Shared tariffs and rules for telegraph and post (ITU, UPU) cut the transaction cost of long-distance trade.

nodes.name: Judicial review
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Leaf within this group; C1 builds its new constitutional_court on it.

prereqAssessment.why: Review presupposes an independent judiciary.

nodes.effectRationale: Laws that violate constitutional rights are struck down instead of enforced.

nodes.name: Trade unions
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds socialism, industrial_arbitration, minimum_wage, workmens_compensation and collective_bargaining.

prereqAssessment.why: Unions bargain over a money wage.
Factory workforces concentrated workers who could combine.
Mule spinners formed some of the first durable unions; the OR with the power loom is right.

nodes.effectRationale: Collective bargaining gives workers a channel for complaint, so grievance builds more slowly.

nodes.name: Limited liability
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds antitrust and deposit_insurance.

prereqAssessment.why: It is a rule of commercial law on creditors' claims.
Limited liability is a privilege of joint-stock companies.

nodes.effectRationale: Small investors can found and back firms without risking ruin, so people rise into the owning class faster.

nodes.name: Mass press
nodes.auditRationale: Replace railway by steam_rotary (or T7 steam_printing_press when integrated): the mass press is a product of steam printing, not of railways.

prereqAssessment.why: The press is the base technology.

The 1833 penny press (and The Times from 1814) depended on steam-driven cylinder presses printing thousands of sheets an hour and sold on city streets; rail distribution came later and is not the enabling input. steam_rotary (1781) is the steam power that drove Koenig's press. If T7's new steam_printing_press is accepted, it is the better atom still.

nodes.effectRationale: Cheap papers carry job advertisements, ship sailings and emigrant letters to every reader, so people move more freely.

nodes.name: Merit civil service
nodes.auditRationale: Replace appointed_officials with civil_service_examinations: it bridges the A6 examination node (whose only dependent is absolute_monarchy) to its modern successor. This group also hangs five A9 administrative nodes on merit_civil_service.

prereqAssessment.why: Northcote-Trevelyan and the Pendleton Act took competitive examination from the Chinese model via the East India Company's Haileybury tests; civil_service_examinations is the causal parent. It already requires appointed_officials, so nothing is lost.
Open competition needs a schooled pool of candidates.

nodes.effectRationale: Open competition opens office to the schooled sons of shopkeepers and clerks: faster promotion.

nodes.name: Nationalism
nodes.auditRationale: Sound; feeds decolonization, fascism and four new nodes.

prereqAssessment.why: The nation as sovereign.
Redundant in closure (social_contract already requires it) but marks the print-language argument; harmless.

nodes.effectRationale: Citizens who identify with the nation accept national taxes and war loans more readily, raising extraction.

nodes.name: Nature conservation
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds environmental_regulation, soil_conservation and fisheries_management.

prereqAssessment.why: Royal forest reserves are the legal precedent for protected land.
Protecting species requires classifying them.

nodes.effectRationale: Protected forests and watersheds buffer floods and droughts, steadying harvests downstream.

nodes.name: Popular sovereignty
nodes.auditRationale: Sound hub.

prereqAssessment.why: Popular sovereignty applies contract theory.
Exercised through representatives.

nodes.effectRationale: A people that holds sovereignty can remove grievances through its representatives.

nodes.name: Freedom of the press
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf in this group; integrators should note C2's new freedom_of_information already depends on it.

prereqAssessment.why: Freedom of the press is defined as abolishing prior licensing.
Rights charters entrench the freedom (1689 precursor, 1791 First Amendment).
Sweden's 1766 act was a fundamental law; OR with bill_of_rights is right.

nodes.effectRationale: Abuses can be printed and answered before they fester: grievance accumulates more slowly.

nodes.name: Professional sport
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate end-state leaf of the spectacle line; kept.

prereqAssessment.why: Professional leagues continue the public contest.
National leagues need teams and crowds to travel between cities weekly.

nodes.effectRationale: Weekly matches give urban workers a licensed outlet and shared loyalty, damping the output cost of unrest.

nodes.name: Public postal service
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; bridged by universal_telephone_service (telephone AND public_postal_service), the same universal-service idea applied to the telephone.

prereqAssessment.why: The public post opens the state's relay network to everyone.
Rail mail made a uniform cheap rate feasible (Penny Post 1840).

nodes.effectRationale: Cheap letters keep emigrants in touch with home and send back prepaid tickets: migration chains reach much further.

nodes.name: Referendum
nodes.auditRationale: Keep as a deliberate leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: Direct decision by voters descends from the assembly.
The referendum is a constitutional procedure.

nodes.effectRationale: Tax morale is higher where voters approve taxes directly (Feld and Frey on Swiss cantons): taxes extract more.

nodes.name: Research university
nodes.auditRationale: Add chartered_universities (new, A6) to make the institutional lineage explicit. The A6 sweep already forces it complete before A8, so this costs no extra pacing.

prereqAssessment.why: Research as a professional duty comes from the societies' experimental culture.
Berlin was a state foundation training state officials; the state-academy model.

(proposed addition) New A6 node in this file: the Berlin model reformed an existing corporate university (faculties, degrees, doctorates); the medieval university is its direct institutional ancestor.

nodes.effectRationale: Paid professors who must publish and train doctoral students raise research yield and bring new universities to maturity faster; the lane's industrial landmark.

nodes.name: Secret ballot
nodes.auditRationale: Keep as a deliberate leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: Victoria introduced the ballot with manhood suffrage; it protects a mass electorate.

nodes.effectRationale: Private, official ballots end election-day intimidation, bribery and riots.

nodes.name: Secular state
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now feeds multiculturalism and modernizing_nationalism.

prereqAssessment.why: Equality of faiths extends toleration.
The First Amendment and 1905 law are constitutional or statutory.

nodes.effectRationale: Offices and universities open regardless of confession (repeal of the Test Acts), so people rise faster.

nodes.name: Settler land grants
nodes.auditRationale: The current AND forbids the node's own anchor case (the US public domain). federal_republic (1787 CE) predates 1862, A7 is earlier than A8; chronology and sweep are safe.

prereqAssessment.why: Land must be surveyed and registered before it is granted.

The emerged anchor (Homestead Act, 1862) was issued by a federal republic with no colonial council; Canada's Dominion Lands Act and Australian selection acts were colonial. Make it an OR with federal_republic.

nodes.effectRationale: Free or cheap surveyed land draws settlers and lets founding parties be larger.

nodes.name: Socialism
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now required by marxist_leninist_state (proposed) and feeds social_democracy, vanguard_party and liberation_theology.

prereqAssessment.why: Workers' movements are the base.
Owenite tracts and the Manifesto spread the movement in print; not implied by labour_unions, so it is a real conjunct.

nodes.effectRationale: Workers' mutual-aid funds and cooperative stores tide households over lost wages and dear bread.

nodes.name: Women's suffrage
nodes.auditRationale: Keep as a deliberate leaf; equal_pay_law (A9) builds on it.

prereqAssessment.why: Extension of an existing franchise.

nodes.effectRationale: Enfranchised women shifted public spending to child health and relief (Miller 2008, US states): children are better protected.

nodes.name: Revolutionary republic
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Founded in the name of the people.
Constitutions of 1791/1793.
The citizen army.

nodes.effectRationale: Careers open to talent: privilege abolished, officers and officials promoted from the ranks.

nodes.name: Arms control
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf at the end of the diplomacy lane.

prereqAssessment.why: Treaty limits are negotiated in the collective-security system (NPT under UN auspices).
The emerged anchor (NPT, SALT) is nuclear. Earlier naval limitation (Washington, 1922) is noted but is not the node's capability.

nodes.effectRationale: Detente opened East-West trade alongside SALT (the 1972 grain agreement), narrowing price gaps.

nodes.name: Civil rights law
nodes.auditRationale: Landmark leaf of the welfare lane.

prereqAssessment.why: Civil rights extend declared rights to protected groups.
Civil rights legislation followed the enfranchisement of the groups it protects.

nodes.effectRationale: Banning discrimination in work and schooling opens promotion to excluded groups and removes a standing grievance.

nodes.name: Climate accords
nodes.auditRationale: Terminal node of the environment lane.

prereqAssessment.why: International limits extend national pollution regulation.
Accords are negotiated within UN bodies.
Climate models grew from numerical weather prediction.

nodes.effectRationale: Limiting warming reduces the frequency of droughts and floods, so harvests vary less.

civ6.analog: Environmentalism (Gathering Storm civic; outside the base-game data file)

nodes.name: Collective security
nodes.auditRationale: Hub: arms_control, integrated_alliance_command and the new peacekeeping_operations.

prereqAssessment.why: League and UN are permanent organisations.
Collective security builds on codified rules of war and aggression.

nodes.effectRationale: A collective guarantee against aggression lowers the risk of invasion and its disorder.

nodes.name: Data protection law
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate end-state leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: The law answers computerized personal databases.
It is framed as a privacy right.

nodes.effectRationale: People can see and correct what states and firms hold on them, removing a standing source of grievance.

nodes.name: Decolonization
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now feeds the new states_reorganisation and indigenous_land_rights.

prereqAssessment.why: Independence movements are national movements.
Self-determination is asserted in international law (UN Resolution 1514).

nodes.effectRationale: Self-government removes a standing colonial grievance; independence and partition also set large migrations moving.

nodes.name: Environmental regulation
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds climate_accords.

prereqAssessment.why: Regulation of pollution extends protection of land.
Pollution standards are health standards enforced by an agency.

nodes.effectRationale: Limits on smoke, effluent and toxins cut deaths from respiratory and water-borne disease.

civ6.analog: Environmentalism (Gathering Storm civic; outside the base-game data file)

nodes.name: Fascism
nodes.auditRationale: Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: Ultranationalism.
A mass movement party.

nodes.effectRationale: Corporatist bodies bind employers and workers to deliver output to the state, raising extraction.

nodes.name: Human rights law
nodes.auditRationale: Keep. Cost 28,130 equals the A9 median; acceptable.

prereqAssessment.why: Universal rights generalize national bills of rights.
The declaration and its monitoring are international.

nodes.effectRationale: Rights declared for every person and monitored abroad restrain the worst abuses at home.

nodes.name: Integrated alliance command

future.system: Politics / Diplomacy - alliances
future.description: allies place forces under a joint peacetime command

future.system: Battle Layer - joint command of formations
future.description: allied formations act under one command

nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf at the end of the military lane.

prereqAssessment.why: NATO is collective defence rather than UN collective security, but it was founded under Article 51 of the UN Charter; kept.
A joint command is an allied general staff (SHAPE).

nodes.effectRationale: Common infrastructure and standardised fuel and transport (NATO pipelines, STANAGs) speed movement across allied territory.

nodes.name: International tribunals
nodes.auditRationale: Keep; C1's transitional_justice builds on it.

prereqAssessment.why: Tribunals try breaches of the laws of war.
International courts are created by international bodies.

nodes.effectRationale: Trials for atrocities replace cycles of revenge after war, so disorder costs less output.

nodes.name: Internet governance
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate end-state leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: The object governed.
ICANN and the ITU are international bodies.

nodes.effectRationale: Stable naming, addressing and rules for a global network let prices and orders travel instantly between markets, closing price gaps faster.

nodes.name: Multilateral trade rules
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds special_economic_zones.

prereqAssessment.why: GATT bound the tariffs that free-trade states had lowered.
Rules are administered by an international body.

nodes.effectRationale: Bound tariffs and dispute settlement keep markets open, so prices converge across borders.

nodes.name: Nuclear deterrence doctrine
nodes.auditRationale: Deliberate leaf.

prereqAssessment.why: Deterrence needs the weapon.
Doctrine and targeting plans are staff products.

nodes.effectRationale: Deterrent programmes drove state funding of physics, computing and rocketry.

nodes.name: Public broadcasting
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; bridged by distance_education ((public_broadcasting OR television) AND mass_higher_education).

prereqAssessment.why: The medium.
Weak (an A3 atom); the licence and charter are state acts, so kept rather than churned.

nodes.effectRationale: A national public service of news, talks and schools programmes raises the society's civic output; sparing CP use.

nodes.name: Science policy
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; bridged by civil_space_agency and open_access_science.

prereqAssessment.why: Grant agencies fund university research.
Setting national research priorities needs statistics of the research system.

nodes.effectRationale: Grant agencies and national priorities raise research yield and build up new universities faster.

nodes.name: State propaganda
nodes.auditRationale: Sound; dependent fascist_state.

prereqAssessment.why: Propaganda ministries were party instruments.
Print route (US CPI 1917).
Broadcast route (1933 ministry); OR is right.

nodes.effectRationale: A controlled flood of news and film mobilizes opinion and smothers strikes and dissent, cutting the output cost of unrest; strong lever, hence 0.04.

nodes.name: Total mobilization
nodes.auditRationale: Was a leaf; now feeds wartime_rationing, civil_defence and strategic_stockpiles.

prereqAssessment.why: Manpower is mobilised through registration.
Allocating labour and materials needs statistics of production.

nodes.effectRationale: War economies draw new workers into industry and raise extraction through war taxes and controls.

nodes.name: Zoning
nodes.auditRationale: Correct; feeds the new transit_authority.

prereqAssessment.why: Zoning extends building law to land use.
New York's 1916 resolution answered the Equitable Building; German zoning (1891) shows other routes existed, but the edge is kept since it is the documented trigger.

nodes.effectRationale: Envelopes and use zones permit apartment blocks where light and air are protected, so dwellings hold more people.

nodes.name: Fascist state
nodes.auditRationale: Government form (leaf). Sound.

prereqAssessment.why: The movement in power.
Mobilization through propaganda.
Redundant in closure (fascism requires it) but harmless.

nodes.effectRationale: Compulsory labour service (Reichsarbeitsdienst, bonifica works) puts more labour into road and path building.

nodes.name: Burial of the dead
nodes.auditRationale: ochre_processing: the oldest burials (Qafzeh) are ochre-stained; ochre is dated ~100 kya, as early as the burials.
nodes.effectRationale: Shared mourning rites absorb the strain a death puts on a small band, so grievance builds more slowly.

nodes.name: Guest right
nodes.auditRationale: gift_exchange: visits to exchange partners require that strangers who come in peace are fed and protected.
nodes.effectRationale: Safe passage through others' land lets migrants travel further.

nodes.name: Initiation of the young
nodes.auditRationale: oral_tradition: the lore taught to initiates is the memorised body of songs and stories. shamanic_ritual: ritual specialists conduct the seclusion and the rite.
nodes.effectRationale: Adult skills in tracking, trapping and fishing are taught to every youth in a set course, so the band's hunters and fishers are better trained.

nodes.name: Fire-stick land management
nodes.auditRationale: fire_making: deliberate burning is a use of controlled fire.
nodes.effectRationale: Fresh regrowth and concentrated game shorten the lean season, so fewer die of hunger in bad years.

nodes.name: Seasonal round
nodes.auditRationale: shelter_hut: a scheduled round returns to known base camps with built shelters.
nodes.effectRationale: A scheduled round exploits a wider territory than a single camp, so the settlement draws on a larger hinterland.

nodes.name: Wayfinding lore
nodes.auditRationale: oral_tradition: routes, landmarks and water sources are memorised and passed on in song and story.
nodes.effectRationale: Remembered routes let explorers range further from home and return.

nodes.name: Division of labour by sex and age
nodes.auditRationale: atlatl: specialised long-range hunting gear for one task group. grinding_stone: plant-processing gear for the other; the split needs both kits.
nodes.effectRationale: A broader, two-track diet means a failed hunt is carried by gathered staples, so households absorb shortfalls they could not before.

nodes.name: Band territories
nodes.auditRationale: gift_exchange: leave to forage on a neighbour's range is asked through exchange partners (hxaro among the Ju/'hoansi); the partnerships come first (~40 kya).
nodes.effectRationale: Reciprocal access to other ranges lets a band ride out a local failure instead of starving: shortfalls are absorbed.

nodes.name: Customary sanctions
nodes.auditRationale: oral_tradition: a sanction works only if the band's norms are shared and remembered, and foragers carry them in stories and sayings (both ~40 kya).
nodes.effectRationale: Standing penalties check bullies and free-riders before quarrels stop the band's work.

nodes.name: Prestige leadership
nodes.auditRationale: gift_exchange: a headman's standing comes from giving. kin_council: he leads by persuading the council of household heads. Both are A1.
nodes.effectRationale: A respected leader can draw a larger following when a group splits to found a new camp, so founding parties are larger.

nodes.name: Hunt leaders
nodes.auditRationale: kin_council: the household heads choose the leader for the season. atlatl: the spear-thrower is the weapon of the communal drive.
nodes.effectRationale: A disciplined mass kill yields a surplus of dried meat that is stored to carry the band through winter, so stores cover more of the year.

nodes.name: Seasonal gatherings
nodes.auditRationale: kin_council: each band's household heads negotiate with the others. gift_exchange: gatherings are where exchange partners meet and goods change hands. Both are in place by ~10 kya and earlier.
nodes.effectRationale: Marriages and adoptions arranged between bands let people move from one group to another.

nodes.name: Food-sharing norms
nodes.auditRationale: fire_making: the kill is cooked and divided at the common hearth; the sharing rule grows around it.
nodes.effectRationale: Sharing pools the band's food, so children of unlucky hunters are fed in lean seasons.

nodes.name: Out-marriage between bands
nodes.auditRationale: gift_exchange: the partners who pass shell and stone between bands are the same networks through which spouses are exchanged.
nodes.effectRationale: Affines in other bands are a refuge in a local famine: families move to their in-laws' country instead of starving in place.

nodes.name: Monumental shrines
nodes.auditRationale: communal_feasts: Göbekli Tepe's builders were fed at great feasts (~9,500 BCE, same date). shamanic_ritual: the enclosures are ritual spaces.
nodes.effectRationale: Organizing many households into fed work parties is the first mass labour mobilization; the same practice serves later communal works such as tracks and causeways.

nodes.name: Barter of staples
nodes.auditRationale: gift_exchange: the older exchange network; cereal_cultivation: a storable staple to offer in exchange.
nodes.effectRationale: Surplus held in store can be traded away at once, so stocks reach those who need them sooner.

nodes.name: Craft specialization
nodes.auditRationale: pottery_open_fired: the first workshop craft; gift_exchange: a demand for crafted valuables beyond the household.
nodes.effectRationale: Exchange for food lets a share of people live by craft, enlarging the specialist class.

nodes.name: Stock friendship
nodes.auditRationale: cattle: the animals placed with partners. gift_exchange: the long-distance partnership is the forager exchange tie turned to livestock.
nodes.effectRationale: Herds split between distant partners survive local drought and epidemics, so each herder keeps and breeds more stock.

nodes.name: Fishing-station rights
nodes.auditRationale: basketry: weirs and traps are wattle work. dugout: the station is reached and worked by boat.
nodes.effectRationale: Secure ownership makes it worthwhile to build and maintain fixed weirs and traps, which take far more fish than line and spear.

nodes.name: Inviolable seed corn
nodes.auditRationale: cereal_domesticated: domestic cereals exist only because seed was kept back and replanted. kin_council: the elders enforce the rule against eating it.
nodes.effectRationale: A protected store of selected seed raises the next crop; this is the stored-seed bonus the granary operand models.

nodes.name: Transhumance
nodes.auditRationale: sheep_goat: herds to move; seasonal_round: the scheduled movement between seasonal places.
nodes.effectRationale: Rotating pastures by season keeps grazing fresh, so herds yield more.

nodes.name: Island colonization voyages
nodes.auditRationale: raft OR dugout: open-water craft. sheep_goat: settlers carry breeding stock to found herds on the island.
nodes.effectRationale: Planned sea crossings carry explorers further per expedition.

nodes.name: Daughter villages
nodes.auditRationale: cereal_cultivation: farmers carry seed to new land. kin_council: the household heads decide who goes.
nodes.effectRationale: Organised fission sends larger founding parties.

nodes.name: Reciprocal work parties
nodes.auditRationale: communal_feasts: the host feeds the workers; mudbrick: house-raising is the commonest task.
nodes.effectRationale: Pooled neighbours raise a house in days, so each dwelling costs less labour.

nodes.name: Compensation for injury
nodes.auditRationale: gift_exchange: compensation is paid in the valuables that circulate as gifts. kin_council: elders fix the price and witness the settlement. Both far earlier than the first written schedule (~2,100 BCE).
nodes.effectRationale: A settled price ends the wrong; the feud that would have festered does not start.

nodes.name: Rights of clearance
nodes.auditRationale: ground_stone_early: the ground axe fells the trees. cereal_cultivation: the cleared plot is sown.
nodes.effectRationale: Households may open new plots further out without asking for an allotment, so the settlement farms a wider area.

nodes.name: Household fields
nodes.auditRationale: cereal_cultivation: fields worth holding exist only once crops are sown (~11,500 BCE). kin_council: the household heads recognize each other's holdings.
nodes.effectRationale: A household that keeps its field next year manures, weeds and walls it: land yields more.

nodes.name: Witnessed agreements
nodes.auditRationale: gift_exchange: obligations between partners precede formal agreements. token_counting: counted tokens record the quantities promised (~8,000 BCE). Both precede the first written witness lists (~2,600 BCE).
nodes.effectRationale: Enforceable deals with strangers let goods move between villages where prices differ.

nodes.name: First-comer precedence
nodes.auditRationale: ancestor_veneration: precedence is claimed through the ancestors who first cleared the land (dated ~9,000 BCE).
nodes.effectRationale: A recognized founding lineage can allot outlying land to newcomers, so a settlement draws on a wider hinterland.

nodes.name: Insignia of rank
nodes.auditRationale: hereditary_rank: insignia mark inherited office (Varna, ~4,500 BCE, same date). copper_native OR gold_silver_native: the earliest regalia are of native copper and gold.
nodes.effectRationale: A recognizable emblem lets a leader's word carry to villages beyond personal acquaintance, so authority reaches further.

nodes.name: Age sets
nodes.auditRationale: cattle: the age-set system is a herding society's way of guarding herds on distant pastures. war_band: the warrior grade grows out of the raiding party.
nodes.effectRationale: The warrior grade lives in outlying cattle camps and patrols the edges of the range, so armed parties see much further around them.

nodes.name: Warrior retinues
nodes.auditRationale: hereditary_rank: a ranked leader keeps the retinue. war_band: the retinue is a permanent war band.
nodes.effectRationale: Armed followers enforce tribute and dues.

nodes.name: Village defences
nodes.auditRationale: war_band: the defenders are the community's armed men. stone_dry OR timber_frame: walls of stone or palisades of timber.
nodes.effectRationale: Defended stores survive raids and are there to relieve hunger.

nodes.name: Big-man polity
nodes.auditRationale: prestige_leadership: the big-man is the achieved leader. communal_feasts: he wins followers by competitive feasting. Both are earlier.
nodes.effectRationale: Households work harder to produce surplus for their leader's feasts (Sahlins), so each farmer produces more.

nodes.name: Segmentary lineage society
nodes.auditRationale: ancestor_veneration: lineages are defined by a common ancestor. kin_council: each segment is run by its elders. Both precede the node.
nodes.effectRationale: Segments bud off and move away as they grow, so people move more freely.

nodes.name: Sodalities
nodes.auditRationale: communal_feasts: the societies meet and recruit at the great feasts. kin_council: they cut across the kin groups whose heads sit in the council.
nodes.effectRationale: A member travelling or moving is lodged and protected by his society in distant villages, so migrants can go further.

nodes.name: Village headship
nodes.auditRationale: kin_council: the head is chosen from and by the household heads. cereal_cultivation: a permanent farming village needs a standing head (~11,500 BCE onward).
nodes.effectRationale: The head calls work parties for ditches, walls and tracks: more path-building per worker.

nodes.name: Bridewealth
nodes.auditRationale: cattle OR sheep_goat: livestock is the usual currency of the payment. kin_council: the elders of both lineages negotiate and witness it.
nodes.effectRationale: Children whose bridewealth has been paid have a whole lineage answerable for them, so in hunger they are fed by uncles and cousins as well as parents.

nodes.name: Communal storehouses
nodes.auditRationale: cereal_cultivation: there must be grain to store; kin_council: a shared store needs an agreed rule of access.
nodes.effectRationale: A pooled reserve lets households ride out a shortfall without going hungry.

nodes.name: Extended-family households
nodes.auditRationale: timber_frame: long post-built houses can shelter several couples under one roof. cereal_cultivation: farming rewards keeping several workers in one household.
nodes.effectRationale: Several related couples share one large dwelling, so the same housing stock holds more people.

nodes.name: Epic literature
nodes.auditRationale: oral_tradition: the epics write down older sung tales; scribal_schools: copied as school texts.
nodes.effectRationale: A shared heroic past recited across cities binds townspeople and rulers to one story.

nodes.name: State pantheon
nodes.auditRationale: organized_priesthood: priests order the gods. cuneiform OR hieroglyphic: the god lists are written. All are earlier than ~2,600 BCE.
nodes.effectRationale: Conquered cities keep their gods inside the victor's pantheon and accept rule confirmed at the high god's shrine, so authority extends further.

nodes.name: Interest-bearing loans
nodes.auditRationale: temple_economy: temples were the first lenders; standard_weights: loans of silver are measured by weight.
nodes.effectRationale: Credit finances caravans to distant markets, so merchants act on price differences sooner.

nodes.name: Investment partnerships
nodes.auditRationale: trade: the long-distance caravan trade the fund finances. hacksilver: capital is pooled and reckoned in weighed metal.
nodes.effectRationale: Standing pooled capital lets merchants buy stocks where they are cheap and move them to market without waiting to raise funds for each trip.

nodes.name: Court upbringing of vassal heirs
nodes.auditRationale: royal_envoys: the princes come as part of the diplomatic exchange with vassal courts. scribal_schools: they are educated alongside court children in the palace school.
nodes.effectRationale: Vassal rulers raised at court know its language and officials and owe it their thrones, so royal authority holds in distant subject lands.

nodes.name: Frontier fortresses
nodes.auditRationale: territorial_kingship: a kingdom with a frontier to hold. appointed_officials: commandants and scribes man the forts.
nodes.effectRationale: Garrisoned forts project the kingdom's authority to its edge.

nodes.name: Royal expeditions
nodes.auditRationale: appointed_officials: the crown appoints and supplies the leader. sail_square OR donkey: by sea or by caravan.
nodes.effectRationale: State-supplied expeditions reach lands beyond the usual range.

nodes.name: Victory stelae
nodes.auditRationale: court_patronage: royal workshops carve them; cuneiform OR hieroglyphic: the inscribed message.
nodes.effectRationale: A public, lasting announcement of royal power deters revolt in the places it stands.

nodes.name: Herding contracts
nodes.auditRationale: temple_economy: temple and palace own large flocks that must be entrusted to herdsmen. wool: the quotas are reckoned in fleeces and lambs.
nodes.effectRationale: Quotas with a share of the surplus give herdsmen a stake in breeding and fleece, so each herder delivers more.

nodes.name: Wage and hire tariffs
nodes.auditRationale: law_code: tariffs are clauses of written law; corvee_labour: organised labour gangs precede hired labour.
